FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Fire Fighting Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 


The term ‘Water Spray’ refers to the use of water in a form having a pre-determined pattern, particle size, velocity 
and density discharged from specifically designed nozzles or devices. 


Water spray systems are usually applied to special fire protection problems since the protection can be specifically 
designed to provide for effective fire control, extinguishment, prevention or exposure fire protection. These systems 
may be independent of or supplementary to other forms of protection. Water spray systems are most commonly 
used to protect processing blocks, processing equipment, structures, flammable liquids and gas vessels, piping and 
equipment, such as transformers, oil switches and some combustible solids, cable trays, cable racks, etc. 


In situations where oil and flammable liquids are stored and/or used in such quantities and in such manner that the 
value of the standard sprinklers in the event of fire is open to question, medium and/or high velocity sprayers may 
be employed in lieu of or in conjunction with sprinklers. This standard is intended to provide a guide as to when 
such systems should be installed, details of their design and performance. 


This standard was first published in 2003 with a view to providing minimum requirements for fixed water spray 
systems based upon sound engineering practices and with assistance from the then Tariff Advisory Committee. 
The earlier version of this standard covered the provision of water supplies, components to be used, installation 
and testing of the system, maintenance, and the extension of existing systems. 


This revision has been take up to include various new technologies that have been developed in the last few years 
and to make it at par with the international practices. All the principles of 2003 version have been retained in this 
version as well, while amplifying the details with due regard to latest technological innovations and improvements 
in the last decade in process technology, storage in case of plants and also in firefighting methodologies. 


The major changes in this revision include the following: 
a) Provisions on drawings and documentation depicting layout of water spray system including water supply 
have been detailed. 
b) Initial considerations for arriving at the number, system and type of water spray technique have been 
included in detail. 
c) New provisions on selection and types of spray nozzle have been included. 
d) New provisions on components of spray system installation have been included. 
e) Water supply requirements for spray systems and necessary pumping arrangements have also been 
included in detail. 
Nothing in this standard prevents introduction of new concepts and technologies, when such systems are at least 


equivalent to various provisions of this standard and backed up by successful full scale fire testing in recognized 
test laboratories where the design criteria and test results have been fully documented. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of the standard is given in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised )’. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off value should be the same as that of specified value in this standard. 


IS 15325 : 2020 


Indian Standard 


DESIGN AND INSTALLATION OF FIXED AUTOMATIC 
HIGH AND MEDIUM VELOCITY WATER SPRAY 
SYSTEM — CODE OF PRACTICE 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard specifies minimum requirements for 
design, installation and maintenance of fixed automatic 
water spray systems in general areas of plants/industrial 
buildings (high hazards, in general), various types of 
storage tanks (containing flammable liquids) in the open 
tankage areas, cable cellars in power stations and large 
power houses, material carrying conveyors, etc. 


1.2 This standard covers only the types of water spray 
nozzles specified in 6 (see 6.2 and 6.3 in particular for 
details). 


1.3 The requirements of this standard are also applicable 
to any addition, extension, repair or other modification 
to an existing water spray system. 


1.4 The requirements of this standard are also applicable 
to the water spray systems also known as deluge 
systems. It is not the intention of this standard to cover 
other types of systems like automatic sprinkler system, 
foam sprinkler system, vapour mitigation system, etc. 


1.5 The requirements are not valid for certain specific 
applications like those on ships, in aircrafts, on vehicles 
and for below ground systems in the mining industry 
and the like. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on 
this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards . 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply. 


3.1 Automatic Detection Equipment — Equipment 
which will automatically detect one or more 
components directly related to combustion, such as 
heat, smoke, flame and other phenomenon, and cause 
automatic actuation of alarm and protection equipment. 


3.2 Automatic Spray System — A special fixed pipe 
system connected to a reliable source of fire protection 
water supply and equipped with water spray nozzles 
for specific water discharge and distribution over 
the surface or area to be protected. The piping 
system is connected to the water supply through an 
automatically actuated deluge valve, which initiates 
flow of water. 
NOTE — Automatic actuation is achieved by operation of 
automatic detecting equipment installed along with water 
spray nozzles. High velocity and medium velocity systems are 
the types. Spray systems designed to actuate when a sensor 
detects a fire; and no interface operation or action by personnel 
is required. 


3.3 Class A Liquid — Liquids having flash point 
below 23°C. 


3.4 Class B Liquid — Liquids having flash point of 
23°C and above but below 65°C. 


3.5 Class C Liquid — Liquids having flash point of 
65°C and above but below 93°C. 


3.6 Combined System — A system of piping that 
connects both hydrant or sprinkler system with the 
water spray system (also called tapped system) and is 
supplied by a common piping and actuation valve. 


3.7 Control of Burning — Application of water spray 
to the source of the fire or fuel surface to reduce the rate 
of burning and heat release from a fire until the source 
of fuel can be shut off, the fire can be extinguished or 
the fuel is all consumed. 


3.8 Deluge Valve — A quick opening system actuation 
valve which allows water to flow into a piping system 
to discharge from all open pipes or spray nozzles. A 
deluge valve can be opened automatically, in response 
to a detection system installed in the area being 
protected or by manual operation in an area remote 
from the fire area. 


3.9 Density — The unit rate of water application to an 
area or surface expressed in litres/min/m? (Ipm/m’). 


3.10 Distribution Pipes — A pipe feeding either a 
range pipe directly or a single sprinkler on a non- 
terminal range pipe more than 300 mm long. 


IS 15325 : 2020 


3.11 Electrical Clearance — The air distance between 
the water spray equipment, including piping and 
nozzles, and un-enclosed or un-insulated live electrical 
components at other than ground potential. 


3.12 Envelope — The three-dimensional space 
enclosing the fire. 


3.13 Exposed Equipment — Equipment subject to fire 
damage, usually from a source other than the equipment 
being protected. 


3.14 Exposure Protection — The absorption of heat 
through application of water spray to structures or 
equipment exposed to a fire or radiant heat from a fire, 
or heat buildup due to sunrays in extreme hot weather to 
limit surface temperature to a level that will minimize 
damage and prevent failure. 


3.15 Extinguishment — Occurs when combustion is 
no longer present. 


3.16 Fire Barrier — A fire barrier is a continuous wall 
or floor that is designed and constructed to limit the 
spread of fire. 


3.17 Fire Proofing — The application of a fire resistant 
material to minimize the effects of fire exposure by 
flame impingement, to reduce the rate of temperature 
rise of the material and to delay heat-induced structural 
failure. 


3.18 Flash Point — The minimum temperature at 
which the liquid gives so much vapour that this vapour, 
when mixed with air, forms an ignitable mixture and 
gives a momentary flash on application of a small pilot 
flame under specified conditions of test. 


3.19 Gauge 


3.19.1 ‘A’ Gauge — Pressure gauge connected to a 
town main connection between the supply pipe stop 
valve and the non-return valve. 


3.19.2 ‘B’ Gauge — Pressure gauge connected to and 
on the same level as an deluge valve, indicating the 
pressure on the upstream side of the valve. 


3.19.3 ‘C’ Gauge — Pressure gauge connected to and 
on the same level as an deluge valve, indicating the 
pressure on the downstream side of the valve. 


3.20 Impingement — The striking of a protected 
surface by water droplets issuing directly from 
projectors and/or sprayers. 


3.21 Insulated Equipment — Equipment, structures 
and vessels provided with insulation which for the 
expected duration of exposure, will protect steel from 
exceeding a temperature of 454°C (850°F) for structural 
members and 343°C (650°F) for vessels. 


3.22 Manual Spray Systems — Spray systems that 
must be actuated by a person. 


3.23 Non-absorbing Ground — Earth or fill that is 
not readily permeable or absorbent to large quantities 
of flammable or combustible liquid or water or both. 


3.24 Pilot Sprinkler — An automatic sprinkler or 
thermostatic fixed temperature release device used as 
a detector to pneumatically or hydraulically release the 
system actuation valve. 


3.25 Range Pipes — Pipes on which sprinklers are 
attached either directly or through short arm pipes, 
which do not exceed 300 mm in length. 


3.26 Run Down Coverage — A protective water 
film flowing down by gravity onto lower portions 
of equipment (such as vessels or towers) from water 
applied to higher portions 


3.27 Slippage — The horizontal component of the 
travel of water along the surface beyond the point of 
contact caused by the momentum of water. 


3.28 Spray Nozzle — A normally open water 

discharging device which, when supplied with water 

under pressure, will distribute the water in a special 

directional pattern peculiar to the particular device. 
NOTE — Nozzles used for high velocity water spray systems 
are called ‘projectors’ and nozzles used for medium velocity 
water spray systems are called ‘sprayers’. Both these nozzles 
are made in a range of orifice sizes with varying discharge 
angles so that designed water density can be achieved for 
optimum protection. 


3.29 Water Wastage — The discharge from water 
spray nozzles that does not impinge on the surface 
being protected. 


4 DOCUMENTATION 


4.1 Preparation of Drawings 


Drawings shall be prepared in accordance to the 
following: 


a) Drawings shall be clear, contain all required 
details including scale and point of compass and 
shall be dated. 


b) Drawings of new installation shall show the entire 
compound; all buildings therein, with their door 
and window openings, and the boundary walls. 
Buildings under construction and future extension 
envisaged shall be indicated by dotted lines. 


c) Drawings of extensions to approved existing 
installations need not show the rest of the 
compound but sufficient details shall be given 
of the existing installations, in correlation to the 
extension, to enable the authorities concerned to 
check the plans and offer comments. 


d) In case of storeyed buildings, drawings submitted 
shall include plans of each storey together with 
sectional elevations. 


e) Drawings shall be on white paper or ammonia 
paper or ferro prussiate paper. 


f) Drawings shall generally be prepared in 
accordance with SP 46, shall not exceed 850 mm x 
1200 mm in size and shall be drawn to a scale 
of 1 : 500 or 1 : 1 000. In the case of very large 
compounds with more than one building, it is 
advisable to submit separate drawing for each risk 
with a key plan showing the relative situation of 
the various buildings, etc, in the compound. 


4.2 Drawings Illustration 


Drawings illustration shall also depict the following 
details: 


a) Pucca walls to be shown by double lines, doors 
and windows being clearly marked. 


b) Iron or other non-masonry walls to be shown by a 
thin line and nature of construction indicated. 


c) Fire walls to be indicated by the sign ‘fire wall’ 
at each end of the wall alongside or across them 
at regular intervals and marked in distinctive 
colours.

wa 


Fireproof doors and/or shutters to be marked as 
follows: 

1) Single fireproof door and/or shutter : ‘SFD’; 
and 


2) Double fireproof door and/or shutter : ‘DFD’ 
Skylights to be marked ‘sky lights’ or ‘SL’. 


f) Boiler to be shown by a rectangular figure marked 
‘boiler’.

clearly indicated, such as ‘mm dia’, lengths of ‘m

j) Pump(s) suction piping to be shown dotted and

n) Fire alarm bells to be shown by a green line, the

be necessary in the case of sprayer installation: 


a) Drawings showing layout of the entire sprayer 
system incorporating material specifications, 
different sizes of mains, etc. 


b) Each sprayer layout drawing shall indicate the

type, K-factor, etc. 


c) Number of sprayers on each deluge valve set. 


d) Height of highest sprayer on each deluge valve

j) Sub-station location in relation to other blocks if 
the pump is electrically driven. 

k) Route of cable from substation to fire pump house. 

m) Schematic circuit line diagram showing electric 
feed to fire pump. 

n) A statement that the system will comply with this 
specification including details of any deviations 
from its recommendations with the reasons for the 
deviations. 

p) A list of the components suitable for sprayer 
use included in the system, each identified 
by manufacturer’s name and model/reference 
number.

4.4.2 Hydraulically Calculated Pipe Work 


For hydraulically calculated pipe work, the following 
shall be given with detailed calculations, either as 
purpose designed work sheets or as a computer print- 
out: 
a) For each design area of operation: 

1) Area identification. 

2) Hazard class. 

3) Specified density of discharge (lpm/m’). 

4) Area covered per sprayer (in m°). 

5) Detailed and dimensioned working drawings 

showing the following: 

i) Node or pipe reference scheme used 
to identify pipes, junctions, sprayer 
heads and fittings which need hydraulic 
consideration; and 

ii) Height above datum of each point of 
identified deluge valve. 

b 


wm 


For each operating sprayer: 

1) Sprayer node or reference number; 

2) Sprayer nominal K-factor and discharge angle; 
3) Flow through the sprinkler (in l/min); and 


4) Inlet pressure to the sprinkler or sprayer 
assembly (in bar). 


c 


wm 


For each hydraulically significant pipe: 
1) Pipe node or other reference; 
2) Pipe nominal bore ( in mm); 
3) Hazen-Williams constant (C or K-factor) for 
the pipe; 
4) Flow through pipe ( in l/min); 
5) Nominal fluid velocity (in m/s); 
6) Length of pipe ( in m); 
7) Numbers, types and equivalent lengths of 
fittings; 
8) Static head change in pipe (in m); 
9) Pressures at inlet and outlet of pipe, in bar; 
10) Friction loss in pipe ( in bar); and 
11) Indication of flow direction. 
NOTE — A line diagram of the pipe layout should be prepared 
showing the following: 
a) node or pipe reference numbers: 
b) distribution pipes, 
c) range pipes, and 


d) sprayer heads under consideration. 


4.5 Water Supply Drawings 


The drawings shall show water supplies and pipe 
work therefrom upto the installation control valves. 
The drawings shall be on an indicated scale of not less 
than 1 : 100. A key to the symbols shall be included. 
The position and type of stop and check valves and 
any pressure reducing valve, water meter, water lock, 
orifice plate and any connection supplying water for 
other services shall be indicated. 


5 INITIAL CONSIDERATIONS 


5.1 Consultation 


Where a spray system or an extension or alteration to 
a spray system is being considered for new or existing 
facilities, the authorities concerned shall be consulted 
at an early stage. 


5.2 Outline Design 
Consideration should be given to any benefits that 
might be gained by changes in building design, work 
procedures, etc, when preparing the outline design. 
In planning site layout and building/tankage design, 
particular consideration should be given to the 
following: 

a) Occupancy which determines the water discharge 

density and water supply pressure, and flow; 

b) Siting of any main water supply connection(s); 

c) Siting of any water supply tank(s) or reservoir; 

d) Siting of any pump house; 


e) The maximum quantity of water available from 
the supply source compared with the system 
requirements 


f) Location of deluge valves together with the access 
thereto; indication of position of valves; and the 
disposal of drainage and water after any test; 


g) Source and means of supply of electric power, etc; 
and 


h) Protection of deluge valves(s), pipe work within 
and outside the plant/tankage facilities against 
accidental damage. 


5.3 It is important to consider building design in the 
context of fire protection, for example, choice of 
materials, support of spray pipe work having regard 
to the load imposed on building structure/tankage by 
the weight of spray pipe work and the contained water, 
need for inbuilt drainage, etc. 


5.4 Design Objectives 
The following objectives shall be considered in the 
design: 
a) Protection with water spray systems shall be 
considered as best option in case of following: 
1) Fire extinguishment, 
2) Control of burning, 
3) Exposure protection, and 
4) Fire prevention. 
b 


wm 


A study shall be made of the physical and chemical 
properties of the materials for which the water 
spray protection is being considered to determine 
the advisability of its use. 

c) The flash point, specific gravity, viscosity, 
miscibility, and solubility and permeability of 
the material, temperature of the water spray, 
and the normal temperature of the hazard to be 
protected are among the factors that shall be given 
consideration. 


d) Where water spray can encounter confined 
materials at a high temperature or with a wide 
distillation range, the slop-over or frothing hazard 
shall be evaluated. 


5.5 Supplementary Information 


The following supplementary information may also be 
considered, as applicable: 


a) Where protecting water soluble materials such as 
alcohol, systems shall be permitted to be designed 
for extinguishment by control, extinguishment 
by dilution or extinguishment by an adequate 
application rate and coverage. 


b) Each water soluble material shall be tested under 
the conditions of use to determine the applicability 
of a water spray system, unless design supportive 


data is available. 


wm 


IS 15325 : 2020 


c) Water spray shall not be used for direct application 
to materials that react with water, such as metallic 
sodium or calcium carbide, which produce violent 
reactions or increase hazardous products as a 
result of heated vapour emission. 


d 


wm 


Water spray shall not be used for applications 
involving liquefied gases at cryogenic temperatures 
(such as liquefied natural gas), which boil violently 
when heated by water. 


e) An evaluation shall be conducted, given the 
possibility of damage, distortion or failure of 
equipment operating at high temperatures due to 
water spray application. 


5.6 Interaction with Other Fire Protection Measures 


Account shall be taken of possible interaction between 
spray systems and other fire protection measures. 
Examples of possible adverse interactions between 
spray protection and other fire protection measures, 
which need specific considerations, are: 


a) Water damage to an inadequately shielded fire 
alarm control panel in a spray protected area 
with consequent possible failure of the fire alarm 
system. 


b 


wm 


Operation or failure of smoke detectors in zones 
adjacent to one in which water discharge has taken 
place because of the water spray mist travelling to 
adjacent zones. 


c 


wm 


It is possible that water spray protection for plant/ 
equipment is independent through dedicated 
pumping facilities or tapped from hydrant 
protection already available in the premises. 
While the design of the system in either case 
shall remain same with regard to provision of 
sprayers, piping, etc pumping capacity and water 
storage requirements for the hydrant system shall 
be suitably increased to take care of additional 
load. 


Determining the need for water spray protection 
at various locations, particularly in petrochemical 
plants, refineries, bottling plants, etc, includes an 
evaluation of the extent and capabilities of other 
types of fire protection both active and passive 
ones. Various options are available to protect 
equipment and shall be explored to determine the 
most suitable approach for a specific hazard or 
area. Major factors to be evaluated include but are 
not limited to the following: 


d 


wm 


1) Fire separation spacing between various plant 
units, equipment, etc. 

2) Fireproofing of building structures and also 
flammable storage tanks inside and outside 
plant battery. 

3) Vertical height of columns and equipment 
where other fire protection measures are not 
possible. 


IS 15325 : 2020 


4) Safe shutdown systems, both manual and 
automatic shutdown. 


5 


wa 


Access to the cluster of equipment due to 
radiant heat, obscured visibility, lack of access 
to hose streams, etc. 


6 


wm 


Safe blow down of flammable liquids and 
vapour phase contents of the plants to blow 
down drums, pits or sumps and/or flare or any 
other safe location. 


7) Response times and capabilities of plant and 
other fire brigades. 
8) Fire hydrant system with pumps, fixed 


monitors, portable monitors and hose streams, 
and foam systems. 


9 


wa 


Prolonged water application facilities to 
facilitate safe shutdown and removal of 
flammables. 
10) The availability of portable and mobile 
firefighting equipment and personnel to 
operate it. 


11 


wm 


Drainage facilities for flammable liquids/ 


hydrocarbon from a spill area. 
12) Hold-up of flammable liquids/hydrocarbon 


inside plants, temperature, and volatility. 
13 


wa 


Protection with passive as well as active 
systems for most critical equipment. 


14 


wa 


Public liability to the adjoining surroundings 
arising out of leakage of flammable and toxic 
chemicals 


e) Such possible interactions need careful 


considerations. 
6 SPRAY NOZZLES 


6.1 General 


Water spray systems are usually applied to special fire 
protection problems beyond the capability of a standard 
sprinkler system. They are specifically designed for 
fire control, extinguishment, prevention or exposure 
protection. These systems typically require that water 
be applied rapidly and uniformly to all protected 
surfaces at the same time, an objective that may not be 
possible with closed nozzles. 


In addition, to protect specific surfaces, the use 
of special nozzles with directional discharge is 
employed. The placement of these nozzles to provide 
proper coverage is often in conflict with the required 
placement to ensure prompt operation where automatic 
nozzles are used. Thus, the standard suggests that open 
nozzles will normally be employed and that a separate 
detection system will be used to actuate the system. 


There are cases, however, where it is desirable to use 
closed nozzles to limit the discharge of water to prevent 
equipment damage (such as when water spray is used 


for local protection of sensitive equipment like turbine 
bearings) or there are environmental concerns. 


Automatic nozzles shall only be used where open 
nozzles present such problems and the position of the 
nozzles can meet both the coverage and response time 
as required under design objectives. 


6.2 Selection of Nozzles 


Nozzles shall be always of open type. Automatic 
(closed) nozzles shall be permitted where positioned 
and located so as to provide satisfactory performance 
with respect to activation time and distribution. The 
selection of the type and size of spray nozzles shall be 
made with proper consideration given to such factors 
as discharge characteristics, physical character of the 
hazard involved, ambient conditions, material likely to 
be burning, and the design objectives of the system. 


Where acceptable to the Authority having jurisdiction, 
sprinklers shall be permitted to be used in water spray 
systems and installed in positions other than anticipated 
by their listing to achieve specific results where 
special situations require. Water spray nozzles can 
be permitted to be placed in any position, within their 
listing limitations, necessary to obtain proper coverage 
of the protected area. The positioning of water spray 
nozzles shall include an evaluation of all the following 
factors: 


a) Shape and size of the area to be protected; 


b) Nozzle design (end connection and material of 
construction) and characteristics of the water 
spray pattern to be produced; 


c) Effect of wind and fire draft on very small drop 
sizes or on large drop sizes with little initial 
velocity; 


d) Potential to miss the target surface and increase 
water wastage; 


e) Effects of nozzle orientation on coverage 
characteristics; and 

f) Potential for mechanical damage. 
6.2.1 Nozzles shall be of the type that has been tested 
and listed for use in water spray systems. The selection 
of specific spray involves consideration of the following 
factors: 

a) Characteristics of the equipment to be protected; 

b) Purpose of the system; 

c) Discharge characteristics of the nozzle; 

d) Possible wind or thermal draft conditions; 

e) Equipment and 
requirements; 


configuration spacing 
f) Corrosive water or atmospheric conditions; 


g) Water flow rate requirements versus availability; 
and 


h) Drainage. 


The effective range of the spray is determined by the 
velocity and the size of the water droplets. Because of 
differences in orifice size, nozzle characteristics, and 
discharge patterns, one type of nozzle cannot ordinarily 
be substituted for another without proper analysis. 


6.3 Type of Nozzles 


Three types of nozzles namely, high velocity, medium 
velocity and drencher type (window and curtain) are 
covered as per this standard, and each of them has 
their own application in protection with water spray 
systems. Design requirements for the same are covered 
in detail in 7 and 8. Nozzles used for high velocity water 
spray systems are called ‘projectors’ and nozzles used 
for medium velocity water spray systems are called 
‘sprayers’. Both these nozzles are made in a range 
of orifice sizes with varying discharge angles so that 
discharge can be controlled for optimum protection. 


6.3.1 Medium Velocity Water Spray System 


Nozzles are generally used for spray angles between 
60° and 140°. They are recommended for usage in 
various applications with different K-factors between 
18 and 100. These nozzles are used in the protection 
of high hazard plant areas, horizontal tanks like 
bullets, spheres, vertical atmospheric fixed and floating 
roof type tanks, conveyors, cable cellars and similar 
applications. 


6.3.2 High Velocity Water Spray System 


Nozzles are generally used for spray angles between 
65° and 150°. They are recommended for usage in 
applications with different K-factors between 18 and 
110. These nozzles are generally used for oil filled 
equipment like transformers and other types of oil 
tanks. 


6.3.3 Drencher Type (Window and Curtain) Nozzles 


Water curtain nozzle distributes water in a flat curtain 
extending all the way to the ground. Water curtain 
nozzle, when mounted in pendent position, acts as a 
window, spray nozzle to protect interior walls, windows 
and other opening of the building which are affected 
by fire. The nozzles, when mounted in horizontal 
position with flow towards ground, a flat water curtain 
are produced to segregate the area which is under fire. 
They are generally used in applications with different 
K-factors, between 20 and 140. 


There are restrictions in choosing K-factor and sprayer 
angle for various types of protection and the same are 
incorporated under each application. 


7 HIGH VELOCITY WATER SPRAY SYSTEMS 


7.1 General 


High velocity water spray systems are installed to 
extinguish fires involving liquids with flash points 


IS 15325 : 2020 


of 65°C (150°F) or higher. Three principles of 
extinguishment are employed in the system, namely, 
emulsification, cooling and smothering. The result 
of applying these principles is to extinguish the fire 
within a few seconds. Guidelines for protection of the 
following are covered hereunder: 


a) Transformers, oil filled equipment of power 
stations; 


b) Turbo-alternators; and 
c) Oil-fired boiler rooms and oil quenching tanks. 


7.2 Transformer Protection 
7.2.1 General 


7.2.1.1 Transformer protection shall contemplate 
on essentially complete impingement on all exterior 
surfaces except the underside, which may be protected 
by horizontal projectors. 


7.2.1.2 Transformers present particular design problems 
for water spray protection, primarily due to their 
irregular shape and necessary clearances to be provided 
for the high voltage equipment. Generally speaking, 
there is much more interference with the water flow 
on the sides of the transformer than at their top. Due 
to this reason, the protection usually involves a large 
number of small capacity projectors than a few bigger 
ones. Often it will be necessary to put more water on 
the transformer than required to achieve complete 
impingement and total envelopment. 


Hence, it is necessary to submit the following 
information with detailed drawings to check the design 
of spray system of a transformer: 

a) Length of the transformer; 

b) Width of the transformer; 

c) Height of the transformer; 

d) Location and height of bushings; 

e) Size and location of oil conservator tank; 

f) Location of switch boxes, tap changing gears and 
other equipment that obstruct and interfere with 
water distribution; 

g) Specification, such as kVA rating, voltage rating, 
oil quantity, etc; 

h) Details showing the direction of incoming and 
outgoing cabling and ducting; 

j) Details of flooring on which the transformer is 
installed and nature of floor around the transformer 
such as concrete, asphalt, pebble filled, etc; 

k) Elevation of transformer above the grade; 

m) Size and location of fire barrier walls; 

n) Siting of radiators and cooler banks in relation to 
the transformer and the surrounding ground level; 

p) Protection and detection piping in different 
colours; and 


IS 15325 : 2020 


q) Projector characteristics showing the ‘K’ factor, 
cone angle, discharge in litres per minute and 
effective reach. 


7.2.1.3 The drawings shall clearly show top, sides 
and bottom of the transformer and also isometric 
views showing all the above details. Also the piping, 
explosion vents, flanges, etc should be clearly shown. 


7.2.1.4 The projection from the surfaces like ribbings, 
tap changers, cable boxes, etc, would ‘roof off’ the 
downward flow of water and hence ‘run down’ cannot 
be automatically considered. Such ‘roofed off’ areas 
will require specific spray coverage with additional 
projectors. 


7.2.2 Electrical Clearance 


All system components shall be so located as to maintain 
minimum clearances from live parts as shown in 
Table 1. ‘Clearance’ is the air distance between 
water spray equipment including piping nozzles and 
detectors and, uninsulated live electrical components at 
other than ground potential. The minimum clearances 
specified in Table 1 are under normal conditions. 
During the operation of water spray system, they are 
intended for use as safe. The values stated are as per 
requirements of SP 30.

7.2.3 Strainers (see also 9.14) 


Pipeline strainers shall be of approved type for use in 
water supply connections. Strainers must be capable 
of removing from the water all solids of sufficient size 
to prevent the spray nozzles from clogging (normally 
3.2 mm perforations are suitable). In addition, the 
strainer must be capable of continuous operation 


without serious increase in head loss, for a period 
estimated to be ample when considering the type of 
protection provided, the condition of the water and 
similar local circumstances. Also, pipeline strainers 
must incorporate a flush out connection. Individual 
strainers for spray nozzles where required must be 
capable of removing from the water all solids of 
sufficient size to obstruct the spray nozzle they serve. 


7.2.4 General Layout and Design 


7.2.4.1 Transformers shall be protected using rings of 
nozzles there around with the top of transformer and 
subsequently rings for every 3 m from top to bottom 
thereof and beneath each continuous obstruction. The 
rings shall not be located at more than | m of the 
transformer. 


7.2.4.2 Projectors shall be employed to spray water 
horizontally at the bottom if the transformer is at more 
than 300 mm above ground level. 


7.2.4.3 In case of transformers surrounded by concrete 
or asphalted surfaces, projectors must be employed in 
such a way as to wash off flammable liquids away from 
transformers. 


7.2.4.4 Piping network shall be planned with more 
flanged connections in such a way that removal of 
transformer is smoothly enabled by removal of very 
few connections. This also will be helpful in restoring 
the protection to the transformer (after servicing) 
without delay or downtime. 


7.2.4.5 Projectors 


a) Projectors shall not be less than 6 mm orifice, 
in size; 

b) Projectors protecting the top shall be aimed at an 
angle so that all of the water impinges upon the 
transformer, the spray pattern targeting either the 
top of the transformer or partly the top and partly 
the sides; 


c) Projectors protecting the vertical sides and the 
bottom of the transformer shall point directly on 
the surfaces to be protected; 


d) Projectors protecting irregular areas shall be 
located for the best coverage; 


e) Projectors protecting the space between 
transformers and radiators and/or space between 
radiators shall be so located as to spray directly 
into the open space; 


f) Where the components of the transformer create 
spaces greater than 400 mm, such surfaces shall 
be individually protected as far as possible; 


g) As far as possible, water spray piping shall not be 
routed across the top of the transformer tank or 
across the face of the transformer cabinet. When 
it is difficult to achieve this, piping shall be routed 


across the top and face of the cabinet subject 
to maintain requisite distance from the live 
electrical components; 


h) Projectors shall cover the conservators, oil pipe 
joints and flanges, and pumps, if any; and 

j) Direct impingement of water spray on energized 
bushings and/or lightning arresters shall 
be permitted only when authorized by the 
manufacturer or by the electrical inspectorate. 


7.2.4.6 Fire barrier walls (Baffle walls) 


Fire barrier walls shall be constructed between the 
transformers/equipment when the aggregate oil 
capacity of the transformer or bank of transformers 
exceed 2 000 | and these walls shall be of either 
355 mm thick brick or 200 mm thick RCC and carried 
at least 600 mm above the highest point of equipment 
to be protected. 


Fire barrier wall shall be constructed between the 
transformers/equipment, which are not spaced at 
distances mentioned in Table 2. 


Table 2 Separating Distances 
( Clause 7.2.4.6 )

v) Over 30 000 15.0 


7.2.4.7 System design 


For control mode, water shall be applied at a rate of not 
less than 10.2 Ipm/m? of the surface area of the entire 
transformer including the bottom surface, radiators, 
conservators, etc. For suppression mode, the density 
applicable shall not be less than 15 Ipm/m’. Density 
may be reduced to 6.1 lpm/m* for spills on the expected 
non-absorbing ground surface area of exposure. The 
following shall also be taken care of: 


a) Projectors on the rings shall be located at not less 
than 500 mm and not more than 800 mm from the 
transformer/equipment surface. 


b) The horizontal distance between the projectors 
shall be maintained in such a way that their spray 
patterns intersect on the surface of transformer/ 
equipment which, in any case, shall not be more 
than 1.5 m. 


Obstructed or ‘roofed off’ portions (see 7.2.1.4) 
of the transformers shall be protected by separate 


c 


wa 


IS 15325 : 2020 


projectors. For this purpose, it will be permissible 
to extend pipes from the nearest ring by means of 
a nipple. The terminal pipes extended from the 
ring mains shall need separate supports if they are 
600 mm or longer. 

d) Where radiators or cooler banks are located at 
more than 300 mm from the surrounding ground 
level, undersides shall be protected by projectors 
pointing upwards. 

e 


wm 


Where radiator/cooler bank are spaced more 
than 300 mm apart and where the transformer is 
separated at a distance of more than 300 mm from 
the radiator/cooler bank, projectors shall be so 
arranged to spray into the space. Projector angles 
shall be so selected that the cone diameters at the 
entrance of space is equal to or slightly larger than 
the space. 


f) For unobstructed vertical surface, the maximum 
vertical distance between projectors shall be 2.5 m. 
However, for obstructed surface the distance shall 
be governed by the nature of obstruction. 


wa 


Nozzles shall be positioned such that the water 
spray does not envelop energized bushings or 
lightning arresters by direct impingement. 


8 


h 


wm 


The system shall be hydraulically so designed 
that the pressure at the hydraulically most remote 
projectors in the network is not less than 3.5 bar in 
case of an outdoor transformer and 2.8 bar in case 
of an indoor transformer. However, the maximum 
pressure in any projector within a network shall 
not exceed 5 bar. The velocity in the feed pipes 
shall not exceed 10 m/s. 


7.2.5 Detection System for Transformers 


Automatic detection equipment shall be so located and 
adjusted as to operate reliably. The location of detectors 
shall be based on several factors, such as nature 
of hazard, air velocity, temperature variations, and 
configuration of the hazard, indoor or outdoor, open or 
closed structures and other variables. For transformers 
the detector sprinklers shall be as close to the shell as 
possible at all places subject to electrical clearance. 


7.2.5.1 Outdoor transformers 


There shall be a ring of detectors around the top of 
the transformer and a second ring around the base. 
The detectors shall be spaced at a maximum of 
2.5 m intervals. The detectors shall be as close to 
the transformer as possible and shall in no case be 
farther than 300 mm therefrom. Additional detectors 
shall be required for specific known hazard points, 
such as tap changers, cable boxes, vents, oil piping, 
etc. Coolers and radiator banks associated with the 
transformer shall also be provided with detectors at 
two levels. The flanges of oil pipes shall be within 
300 mm from detectors. The conservator tanks shall 
be provided with detectors at 2.5 m spacing. It is 


IS 15325 : 2020 


sufficient to install detectors under the conservator 
tanks. 


Piping shall be individually supported as far as 
possible. Transformer ribbings may be used to support 
the piping. In no case, shall the piping be supported on 
body of transformer. Terminal pipes (other than those 
for projectors protecting ‘roofed off’ portions) longer 
than 300 mm shall be supported separately. Piping 
shall be individually supported as far as possible. 
Transformer ribbings may be used to support the 
piping. In no case shall the piping be supported on the 
body of the transformer. 

NOTE — Pipe work is likely to be affected by stray magnetic 


fields that can produce inductive heating if there is a continuous 
metallic ring. Hence, continuous ring mains shall be avoided. 


7.2.5.2 Indoor transformers 


Where the transformer cubicle is open fronted, the same 
shall be treated as an outdoor transformer with detectors 
as per 7.2.5.1. Where the transformer cubicle is more 
than 6 m in height, the detectors shall be positioned 
as close to the transformer as possible to the top of 
the transformer. Where the transformer cubicle is less 
than 6 m in height, the detectors shall be positioned in 
accordance with IS 15105, that is, ata maximum spacing 
of 4 m with an area coverage of not more than 12 m’. 


7.3 Miscellaneous Protection 


7.3.1 High velocity water spray systems are also 
provided for the protection of following areas in power 
stations: 


a) Inside turbo alternator sets; 

b) Clean and dirty oil tanks, paraffin tanks; 
c) Inside turbo alternator sets; and 

d) Hydrogen cooling and seal oil systems. 


7.3.2 The protection is normally localized and hence 
deemed as ‘spot’ protections as only equipment are 
protected and not the whole area where the equipment 
is installed. The details of design for protection of 
above areas shall be submitted to concerned authorities 
in advance showing the layout of equipment, their 
configuration, location of projectors and detectors, etc, 
along with detailed drawings for prior approval. 


8 MEDIUM VELOCITY WATER 
SYSTEMS 


SPRAY 


8.1 General 


8.1.1 Medium velocity water spray systems are installed 
to control the burning and to provide cooling and/or 
exposure protection to such risks where extinguishment 
is always not possible or even desirable, for example, 
fires involving flammable fluids having flash points 
below 65°C (150°F). These systems are also used 
sometimes for power station applications in coal 
conveyors, cable galleries, etc. 


10 


8.1.2 Guidelines for protection of the following areas 
by medium velocity water spray system are covered 
hereunder: 


a) General area protection (working plants like LPG 
bottling plants, chemical/petrochemical plants 
where flammable solvents are stored and/or used, 
etc); 

b) Horizontal storage vessels (for example, LPG 
bullets, etc); 

c) Vertical storage vessels (for example, benzene, 
xylene and toluene tankage); 

d) Spherical storage vessels (for example, LPG 
bullets, spheres, etc); 

e) Spot protection (protection of selective areas/ 
equipment); 

f) Material carrying conveyors for coal, coke, etc; and 

g) Cable cellars, cable galleries in large power plants 
and power stations. 


8.2 General Area Protections 


8.2.1 Definition 


A process plant where flammable liquids are contained 
in vessels and/or pipes forming a large or small complex 
of the plant either in a room or outdoors or under a 
roof with open sides would be classified as a ‘general 
area’. A plant wherein more than 1 000 | of flammable 
liquids/solvents are stored in small containers would 
also be classified as a ‘General area’. 


8.2.2 General Information 
The density of water application shall depend upon the 
type of flammable liquids handled in the plants and also 
upon the object of protection and site conditions. The 
examples include: 

a) Controlled burning of spilt liquid; 

b) Exposure protection of plant and its structure; 

c) Ceiling height of the risk; 

d) Area of the fire involved; and 

e) Type of containers holding the flammable liquid. 


8.2.3 General Requirements 


8.2.3.1 Sprayers installed at ceiling level shall provide 
general area protection for spill fires and of un-insulated 
structural steel columns/trusses upto 3 m from the 
ceiling sprayers. 


8.2.3.2 If the ceilings or roofs are of either A.C. sheet 
or G.I. sheet and the like or combustible materials, 
additional open type sprinklers shall be provided 
exclusively to protect them with a degree of wetting. 


8.2.3.3 Where the height of ceiling/roof of the plant 
exceeds 13 m from the flooring below, conventional 
open type sprinklers shall be employed instead of 
sprayers. 


8.2.3.4 Vessels, drums, pumps, valves, manifolds and 
flammable liquid pipes inside the plant shall need to be 
protected by sprayers installed at a lower level. 


8.2.3.5 If there are obstructions extending below the 
ceiling sprayers and they are more than | m in width, 
undemeath of such obstructions shall be protected by 
local sprayers. 


8.2.3.6 Structural steel work supporting access 
platforms, catwalks, ladders, etc, may be protected by 
separate sprayers. 


8.2.3.7 As far as possible, the sprayers installed at 
lower levels (see 8.2.3.4, 8.2.3.5 and 8.2.3.6) shall be 
provided with baffle plates. 


8.2.3.8 Full detailed drawings of the following shall be 
submitted along with the proposal: 


a) Plan and sectional views of the risk, floor wise, 
showing the dimensions of the block, equipment 
layout, nature of floors/roof, minimum and 
maximum ceiling height, etc. 

b) Columns, beams and trusses of the supporting 
structure. 

c) Working details of sprayers, sprinklers, detectors, 
their piping, their spacing, zone division, etc; 

d) Location of deluge valves, piping, detector piping 
and their sizes. 

e) Typical mounting arrangements of sprayers, 
sprinklers, detectors, etc. 


y 4 


IS 15325 : 2020 


f) Separate drawing showing the various nodes only 
for hydraulic calculation; 


g) Characteristic curves of sprayers and sprinklers 
showing their pattern, orifice size, K-factor, spray 
angle, discharge in lpm, etc; 

h) Full details of the liquids handled indicating their 
quantity, chemical properties etc. 


j) Up-to date block plan showing clearly the 
distances between various blocks, underground 
tank, mains and their size, detector mains, deluge 
valves, pump house, water reservoir, etc. 


k) A detailed note on the protection scheme 
elucidating the design philosophy. 


8.2.4 Design Density 


8.2.4.1 Design application rates are based on the 
intended exposure protection, control of burning or 
extinguishment objectives. Various clauses in this 
section provide more specific guidance based on the 
actual equipment or structure being protected. These 
parameters shall be discussed and agreed to by the user 
and authorities having jurisdiction. 


8.2.4.2 The density of water application depends upon 
the flash point of the liquids handled and also the 
ceiling height of the building/structure. The correct rate 
of density shall be derived from Fig. 1. 


8.2.4.3 The density obtained from Fig. 1 shall be loaded 
by the fire area factor calculated as below where ‘a’ is

8.2.5 Layout of Protection Network 


8.2.5.1 The discharge cone angles of sprayers shall be 
selected from Fig. 2, which relates height of risk with 
the required angle. Any angle within shaded area is 
deemed acceptable. 


NOTES 
1 It is preferred to use wider angled sprayers at the roof 
according to increase in heights beyond 5 m but within 13 m. 


2 Where heights of less than a metre are encountered, sprayers 
with discharge cone angles of 100° shall only be installed. 


3 If the height of the risk exceeds 13 m, conventional sprinklers 
(open type) shall be installed. 


8.2.5.2 The discharge cone angles of the sprayers shall 
be selected from Fig. 2 which relates height of the risk 
with the required angle. Any angle within the shaded 
area is deemed acceptable. 


8.2.5.3 There shall be at least one sprayer for each 9 m? 
floor area. 


8.2.5.4 The distance adjoining sprayers shall not exceed 
3 m anywhere. 


8.2.5.5 The distance between the last sprayer and the 
external wall or limits of the area shall not exceed 
1.5 m anywhere. 


8.2.5.6 The sprayer piping shall be installed along 
the slope of the roof (in case of sloping roof) but the 
sprayers shall discharge water on the risk in a vertical 
pattern. 


8.2.5.7 In case of grating floors or perforated floors, 
the general area protection as per Fig. 1 shall be 
provided under the lowest floor. Under other floors, the 
sprayers shall be provided to discharge the floor below 
equipment, structural steel, etc at a rate of not less than 
10.2 Ipm/m?. 


NOTE — Incase of R.C.C. floors, each floor shall be protected 
at the same density as determined in 8.2.4.1. 


8.2.5.8 Equipment protection 


If the tops of the vessels are more than 5 m below the 
ceiling and/or platform, individual local protection shall 


12 


be provided by sprayers at a density of not less than 
10.2 Ipm/m? to cover top and sides thereof. Any 
obstructions below the ceiling sprayers, if exceeding 
1 m in width, shall be protected underneath by 
individual sprayers at the same density. 


Similarly, under surface of vessels and equipment, if 
raised 300 mm above the floor level, shall be wetted by 
individual sprayers at the same density. Highly exposed 
critical pipe racks, fin fan coolers, control equipment, 
valves, manifolds and other protuberances shall be 
totally wetted by local sprayers at the 10.2 Ipm/m/?. In 
case of fin fan coolers, nozzles shall be provided at the 
bottom of the fans also, spraying water upwards. 


8.2.5.9 Pumps and compressors 


Pumps that handle flammable liquids or combustible 
liquids at temperatures elevated above their flash 
points and also hot pumps handling hydrocarbons at 
and above 90 percent of their auto-ignition point which 
are located within process structures shall need to be 
protected when following conditions exist: 


a) Liquid being handled is at a temperature that is 
significantly above its flash point and/or is at a 
temperature equal to or above its auto-ignition 
point; 

b) Considered pump is in close proximity to 

other equipment (including adjacent pumps) or 

structures that could be quickly damaged by the 
pump fire; and 

c) Pump is located where protection by monitors or 

hose streams would be difficult or impractical. 


The water spray system should be designed to envelope 
the entire pump including the shaft, seals and other 
critical parts. Optionally, the spray envelope may be 
extended 750 mm beyond the pump periphery, and 
includes suction and discharge parting flanges, check 
valves, gauge connections, block valves, balance lines 
and lubrication connections. 


The application rate should be not less than 
20.4 Ipm/m? of the projected envelope area at grade 
level. Spray nozzles shall be so placed as to cover 
the entire envelope as stated above and the deflectors 
shall not be at more than 1 m from the pump and allied 
equipment. Protection to the compressors handling 
flammable gases shall follow the same philosophy as 
of pumps stated above. 


8.2.5.10 Structural protection 


In all cases, the load bearing structural steelwork for 
the plant and the roof, at levels exceeding 3 m below 
the sprayer at ceiling level, shall be wetted at a rate of 
not less than 10.2 Ipm/m? over the surface area of the 
structural members. 


Columns and beams shall be wetted on each side of 
the steel sections by staggering the sprayers. Any other 
structural steel work (whether load bearing or not) 
which can be subjected to flame impingement shall also

NOTE — Uninterrupted ‘run down’ upto 3.7 m below the level 
of sprayers is permissible. 


8.2.5.11 Roof protection 


To provide wetting for the roof, conventional open type 
sprinklers (preferably) or sprayers shall be installed in 
such a way that there is at least one sprinkler/sprayer for 
every 9 m° area of the roof. Layout of such sprinklers/ 
sprayers shall be in accordance with those for sprayers 
as stated in 8.2.5.2 and 8.2.5.3. Sprinklers/sprayers 
shall be installed normal to the roof and piping shall be 
laid along the roof (in case of sloping roof). 


8.2.5.12 Miscellaneous protection 


Design densities for certain other high hazard 
occupancies shall be as per the following: 


a) LPG bottling plants see 8.2.4.2 
and 8.2.4.3 

b) LPG pump house 20.4 Ipm/m? 

c) LPGcylinder storage 10.2 Ipm/m? 
(empty, filled, cold repair) 

d) LPG tank, truck/tank, 10.2 Ipm/m? 
wagon, loading/unloading 
gantries 

e) Hydrocarbon truck/rail 10.2 Ipm/m? 
loading/unloading racks 

8.2.6 System Hydraulics 


For the protection of large areas, it is permissible to 
divide the building/area into several zones of not less 
than 6 m and not more than 8 m in width and all zones 
in plan view of the risk falling within 6 m from any 
point within a zone shall operate simultaneously. Each 
zone shall be controlled by an individual deluge valve 
and flow through the valves shall not be more than what 
is specified in 9.9.3 and Table 7. Each zone shall be 
so designed that the pressure at the hydraulically most 
unfavourable sprayer/sprinkler is not less than 1.4 bar 
and that at the most favourable sprayer/sprinkler is not 
more than 3.5 bar, and that the velocity in distribution 
pipes shall not exceed 5 m/s. 


Detailed hydraulic calculations in support of the above 
shall be submitted to the Authority for each zone. Orifice 
plates, if required, shall be fitted just above the deluge 
valves to keep pressures within the above limits. The 
aggregate pumping capacity shall be determined by the 
largest demand arising out of combination of deluge 
valves when zones concerned operate simultaneously. 


8.2.7 Detection System (see also 9.15) 


The installation and layout of detection system shall 
be governed by the layout of the water spray system. 


14 


The detection network shall be similar to the sprayer 
network and there shall be same number of detectors as 
there are number of sprayers. The detection piping shall 
be independently supported as far as possible and care 
shall be taken not to support other pipes on detection 
network. Where the building is divided into several 
zones, there shall be a cross zoning of detectors to 
enable simultaneous operation of all zones (see 8.2.6). 


8.2.8 Supporting methods for pipes in case of both the 
detection and sprayers shall preferably be in accordance 
with 9.4 in all respects. 


8.2.9 Pumping Capacity 
Flow requirements as calculated in 8.2.6 shall be 
considered as total pumping discharge requirement and 


pump parameters shall be accordingly determined as 
per 10.1 (c) and Table 8. 


8.2.10 Strainers 
See 7.2.3 and 9.14. 


8.2.11 Water Supply 
See 11.1 and Table 9. 


8.3 Horizontal Cylindrical Storage Tanks 


8.3.1 Proposal for the protection of horizontal vessels 
shall be accompanied by full detailed dimensional 
working drawings showing the following: 


a) Plan, elevation and end view; 

b) Site plan showing the location of all vessels, their 
spacing, etc; 

c) The protuberances, such as valves, drains, 
manholes, flanges, ladders, supporting legs, etc; 


d) Bund area and product pipes within; 


e) Protection and detection piping in different 
colours; and 


f) Sprayers’ characteristics showing the K-factor, 
cone angle and discharge, in lpm. 


8.3.2 General Requirements 


8.3.2.1 The complete exposed area of the horizontal 
storage vessel shall need to be protected at a uniform 
density of water application. 


8.3.2.2 It is also necessary to protect the supporting legs 
and the product pipes within the bund area (if provided) 
by sprayers. 
NOTES 
1 Supporting steel members need not be protected if they are 
300 mm or shorter in height. 
2 Where tankage area is not provided with bund walls, product 
pipes within 15 m of tank shell shall be protected by the sprayers. 
3 Also other occupancies, such as pump house, loading shed, 
etc falling within 15 m of the tank shell shall be protected by 
the sprayers. 


8.3.2.3 The protection network shall be fabricated in 
the form of horizontal rows of sprayers connected by 
piping in rings. The number of rows required shall be 
governed by the diameter of the vessel in accordance 
with Table 3.

8.3.2.9 Vessels shall be spaced at more than 15 m

and water requirements. If this is not followed, the 
aggregate water demand for all such vessels falling 
within the prescribed distance of each other shall be 
the determining factor. 


8.3.3 Sprayer Network Design 


8.3.3.1 Water shall be applied at a minimum density 
of 10.2 Ipm/m? of the exposed area of the vessel. The 
supporting legs and product pipes within the bund shall 
also receive water at the same density. 


NOTES 


1 Supporting steel members need not be protected if they are 
300 mm or shorter in height. 


2 Where tank age area is not provided with bund walls, product 
pipes within 15 m of tank shell shall be protected by the 
sprayers. 

3 Where high wind velocity is expected, for example, near 
sea coasts, the sprayers protecting the tankages shall be 
necessarily installed at 0.45 m from the surface of the vessels 
(see 8.3.2.4). 


8.3.3.2 Number of rows shall depend on the diameter of 
the vessel and they shall be distributed equally around 
the circumference of the vessel (see 8.3.2.3). 


8.3.3.3 Distribution of sprayers on each row
