8.3.3.7 Separate sprayers shall be installed to provide 
wetting of all protuberances from the vessel, such as 
manholes, vents, flanges, relief valves, ladders, etc, in 
addition to the sprayers in rows and ends. 


8.3.3.8 Un-encased steel supports for the vessels 
if exceeding 300 mm in height shall be wetted by 
individual sprayers. 
NOTE — Concrete and encased steel supports need not be 
wetted separately as they are likely to be wetted by the splash 
of water spray for the vessels. 


8.3.3.9 Spacing of sprayers for product pipes within the 
bund shall not exceed 3 m and sprayers shall be at a 
distance of not more than 800 mm from the pipes. 


8.3.4 Piping Layout and Supports 


8.3.4.1 The main feed pipes from the deluge valve 
feeding the network shall be supported at every 3.5 m 
of its run. 


18 


8.3.4.2 Vertical feed pipes shall be provided to establish 
flow from bottom rings to top rings at intervals not 
exceeding 3.5 m along the vessels. These pipes may 
also be used as supporting pipes for the network. 


8.3.4.3 To ensure mechanical stability, good appearance 
and hydraulic gradient, the rings of pipe-work shall be 
of uniform size throughout each ring. 


8.3.4.4 Where it is not possible to independently 
support the protection pipe-work, support can be 
arranged from the protected vessel if plate thickness of 
the vessel is adequate. In such case, synthetic elastomer 
insertion shall be provided beneath the base of support 
to accommodate curvature of the vessel and to prevent 
corrosion. 


8.3.4.5 The sprayers in the bottom ring shall point 45° 
upwards and water in the pipe-work shall never drain 
through the sprayers. 


8.3.4.6 Where vertical feed pipes are used for supporting 
the network, the pipes shall be braced together suitably 
at mid-heights to prevent buckling. 


8.3.4.7 All vertical support pipes shall be fitted with 
non-ferrous or stainless steel cooling/drain/orifice 
plugs. The orifice diameter of hole in the plug shall not 
be less than 3 mm. 


8.3.4.8 Vertical feed pipes, when used as supporting 
pipes, shall be flanged at the, base and bolted securely 
to the ground. 


8.3.4.9 For vessels longer than 10 m in length, the 
network piping shall be so arranged that there is one 
feed pipe into the lower ring from the deluge valve for 
every 10 m and part thereof. It shall be ensured that 
each such segment serve an equal amount of protection 
for hydraulic balance. 


8.3.5 System Hydraulics 


The system shall be so designed that the hydraulically 
most unfavourable sprayer operates at a pressure of not 
less than 1.4 bar and the most favourable sprayer at a 
pressure of not more than 3.5 bar. Calculations along 
with nodal drawings shall be submitted to substantiate 
the above (see also 8.3.2.9). 


8.3.6 Detection System 


8.3.6.1 Detectors shall be installed in horizontal rows 
along the vessels and there must be same number of 
rows as for the sprayers. 


8.3.6.2 Spacing of detectors on rows shall not exceed 
2.5 m. 


8.3.6.3 The detectors shall be located at not more than 
1 m from the shell. 


8.3.6.4 Separate detectors shall be provided for 
protuberances from the shell like manholes, flanges, 
etc. 


8.3.6.5 Detectors shall be so positioned that they will 
not interfere with the spray pattern of the sprayers 
anywhere. 


8.3.6.6 One central row of detectors shall be allowed 
for two vessels with longitudinal axes parallel provided 
guidance as in 8.3.6.3 is adhered to. However, the vessels 
concerned shall be wetted simultaneously during a fire. 


8.4 Vertical Cylindrical Storage Tanks 


8.4.1 Proposals for the protection of vertical vessels 
shall be accompanied by full detailed dimensional 
working drawings showing the following: 

a) Plan, elevation and end view. 


b) Site plan showing the location of all vessels, their 
spacing, etc. 


19 


IS 15325 : 2020 


c) The protuberances, such as valves, drains, 
manholes, flanges, ladders, supporting legs, etc. 


d) Bund area and product pipes within. 


e) Protection and detection piping in different 
colours, 


f) Sprayers’ characteristics showing the K-factor, 
cone angle and discharge, in Ipm. 


8.4.2 General Requirements 


8.4.2.1 The complete exposed area of the vertical 
storage vessel shall need to be protected at a uniform 
density of water application. 


8.4.2.2 It is also necessary to protect the product and 
pipes within the bund area (if provided) by sprayers. 


NOTES 

1 Where tankage area is not provided with bund walls, product 
pipes within 15 m of tank shell shall be protected by the 
sprayers. 

2 Also other occupancies such as pump house, loading shed, 
etc, falling within 15 m of the tank shell shall be protected by 
the sprayers. 


8.4.2.3 The protection piping network shall be 
fabricated in the form of horizontal rings at regular 
intervals and vertical feeder mains. 


8.4.2.4 In case of vertical obstructions like wind 
girders, separate ring(s) shall be provided, if deemed 
necessary. 


8.4.2.5 The conical/flat roof shall also be protected 
by water spray system. For this purpose, sprayers 
shall be connected through an explosion relief valve 
assembly, which enables sprayer piping on top of the 
vessels to be blown off in the event of an explosion 
without obstructing the sprayers cooling on the 
vertical sides. 


8.4.2.6 Vertical mains shall be solely used as feeder 
mains only and sprayers shall be installed on the 
horizontal rings. 


8.4.2.7 The sprayers shall not be less than 6 mm in 
orifice and shall normally have cone angles between 
90° and 125° for vertical sides. For the conical roof/ 
flat roof, wider angle sprayers with higher K-factor is 
recommended to reduce the number of sprayers and 
consequently the weight of piping over the tank. 
NOTE — Sprayers with cone angles less than 90° and 
K-factors less than 26 are permissible for local protection such 
as protuberances. For product piping, it is permissible to use 
wide-angled sprayers more than 125°. 


8.4.2.8 Minimum and maximum operating pressures in 
the network shall be 1.4 bars and 3.5 bars, respectively. 


8.4.2.9 ‘Run down’ shall be considered provided there 
are no obstructions on the sides. For this purpose, 
sprayers with reduced orifice size shall be acceptable in 


IS 15325 : 2020 


the lower rings subject to maintaining uniform density 
all over (see also 8.4.2.4). 


8.4.2.10 Sprayers shall be installed normal to the 
exposed area of the vessel and positioned at a distance 
of not less than 450 mm or more than 650 mm from the 
surface. 


8.4.2.11 Vessels shall be located in individual dykes 
and spaced 15 m (or the diameter of the largest tank if 
the same is more than 15 m) apart. In such cases, the 
water requirement of the largest vessel shall determine 
the pumping and storage requirements. 


However, if a number of tanks are located in a common 
dyke, the tanks located in a common dyke which have 
the largest aggregate shell surface area shall determine 
the pumping and storage requirements. 


In case of tanks located in separate dykes, but within 
a distance of 15 m (or diameter of the larger tank is 
less than 15 m) of each other, the shell surface area of 
all such tanks shall determine the pumping and storage 
requirements. 


NOTES 


1 In case occupancies like pump house, loading sheds, etc, 
exist within 15 m (or the diameter of the largest tank as the 
case may be) of the vessels, such occupancies shall also be 
protected by sprayers. 


2 Normally tanks with Class A and Class B liquids shall need 
to be protected with water spray systems. However, tanks 
containing other types of liquids if, located in a cluster along 
with tanks containing class A/class B liquids, shall also need to 
be protected with water spray system. 


8.4.3 System Design 


8.4.3.1 Density of discharge 


Water shall be applied at a rate of not less than 
10.2 Ipm/m? of the exposed area of the tank shell and 
the roof. The product pipes within the bund shall also 
receive water at this density. 


NOTES: 

1 Supporting legs, if any, shall also receive water at the same 
density irrespective of whether they are insulated or not. 

2 See 8.4.2.2. 


8.4.3.2 Distribution of sprayers 


Sprayers shall be spaced at not more than 2.5 m in the 
rings when measured along the curved surface of the 
vessels. There shall be a ring for every 3.5 m height 
of the shell (see also 8.4.2.4). Due diligence shall be 
exercised about the presence of wind girders and if 
there are more wind girders, at least one ring shall be 
available between the girders subject to 3.5 m distance. 


Sprayers in each successive ring shall be staggered for 
better coverage. Sprayers protecting the roof must be 
located in such a way that the extremities of their spray 
pattern shall at least meet. Separate sprayers shall be 
installed to provide wetting of all protuberances from 
the vessels, such as manholes, flanges, ladders, vents, 


20 


etc. Spacing of sprayers for product pipes within the 
bund shall not exceed 3 m and sprayers shall be at a 
distance of not more than 800 mm from the pipes (see 
also note under 8.4.2.7). 


8.4.4 Piping Layout and Supports 


The main feed pipes from the deluge valve feeding 
the network shall be supported at every 3.5 m of its 
run. The number of vertical feeders for the sprayer 
network depends upon the size of vessel and its height. 
As a good practice, minimum of two such feeders shall 
be provided. However, for the vessels less than 10 m 
diameter and height, one feeder shall be accepted. The 
top ring shall be installed just below the top of the vessel 
and the bottom ring shall be installed at not more than 
2 m from the ground level. The rings may be supported 
on the vessel if plate thickness of the vessel is adequate. 


The vertical feed mains shall also be used as supporting 
pipes. These pipes shall be flanged at the base and 
bolted securely to the ground. The sprayers at the 
bottom ring shall point slightly upwards and water in 
the pipe work shall never drain through the sprayers. 
All support pipes shall be fitted with non-ferrous or 
stainless steel cooling/drain orifice plugs. The orifice 
size of the hole in the plug shall not be less than 3 mm. 


8.4.5 System Hydraulics 


The network shall be hydraulically so designed as 
to provide a minimum running pressure of 1.4 bar at 
the hydraulically most un-favourable sprayer and not 
more than 3.5 bar at the hydraulically most favourable 
sprayer in the network (see also 8.4.2.11). The velocity 
in the feeder pipes shall not exceed 5 m/s when sprayers 
discharge at their nominal rates. 


Detailed hydraulic calculation along with nodal 
drawings shall be submitted supporting the design. 
Orifice plate shall be provided, if required, above 
the deluge valves to meet the conditions as above. 
Flow through the cooling/draining pipes shall also be 
considered for the hydraulic calculation. 


8.4.6 Detection System 


Detectors shall be installed in horizontal rings 
supported on the spray network if necessary. Provision 
of detectors in rings shall comply with the following: 


a) Fixed roof tanks located in separate dykes — 
There shall be at least two rings of detectors, one 
at the top where the conical roof rests and one at 
the bottom within | m from the bottom of the tank 
plate. 


b) Fixed roof tanks located in a cluster within a single 
dyke — There shall be an additional ring over and 
above what is suggested in (a) in the centre of the 
tank height. 


c) Floating roof tanks containing class A liquids — 
There shall be at least two rings of detectors one 


near the top of the tank and one at the bottom 
within 1 m from the bottom of the tank plate 
subject to the condition that detection of fire from 
the mandatory automatic foam system (rim seal 
protection), triggers the water spray system also 
through alarm system interface. 


d) Floating roof tanks containing other than class 
A liquids — There shall be at least three rings of 
detectors, one each at the top of the tank, one at the 
bottom of the tank plate and it is strongly advised 
to provide one at the centre of the tank height (see 
Note 2 under 8.4.2.11) 


e) Fixed and floating roof tanks — In all the cases 
discussed above, spot detectors shall be provided 
for all the protuberances where applicable like, 
manholes, vents, flanges, relief valves, etc, on the 
conical roof as well on vertical sides. 


The spacing of detectors in rings shall not be at more 
than 3 m when measured along the curved surface of the 
vessel. For conical roof the detector shall be installed 
on 9 m’ area basis. The detectors shall be located at not 
more than | m from the shell. Separate detectors shall 
be provided for protuberances like manholes, flanges, 
etc. Detectors shall be so positioned as not to interfere 
with the sprayer pattern of the sprayers anywhere. 
Floating roof tanks storing class A and B liquids shall, 
in addition to the detectors as stated above, shall be 
provided with suitable detection facilities at the floating 
rim seal like linear heat sensing cables as per IS 2189. 


8.5 Protection of Spherical Vessels 
8.5.1 Drawings 


8.5.1.1 Proposals for the protection of vertical vessels 
shall be accompanied by full detailed dimensional 
working drawings showing the following: 


a) Plan, elevation and end view; 

b) Site plan showing the location of all vessels, their 
spacing, etc.; 

c) Protuberances, such as valves, drains, manholes, 
flanges, ladders, supporting legs, etc; 

d) Bund area and product pipes within; 


e) Protection and detection piping in different 
colours; and 


f) Sprayers’ characteristics showing the K-factor, 
cone angle and discharge in lpm. 


8.5.1.2 Spherical vessels are almost certain to be 
pressure vessels. The complete exposed area sphere 
shall need to be protected at a uniform density of water 
application. 


8.5.1.3 It is also necessary to protect the supporting 
legs and the product pipes (for a distance of at least 
15 m from the surface of the sphere) by the water spray 
system at the same density. 


IS 15325 : 2020 


8.5.1.4 The protection network around such vessels 
shall be fabricated in the form of horizontal and/or 
vertical rings at regular intervals. 


8.5.1.5 The sprayers shall not be less than 6 mm in 
orifice size for spheres upto 12 m diameter and more 
than 6 mm for those having diameters more than 12 m. 
The sprayers shall normally have cone angles between 
90° and 125° for covering the spherical surface. 
NOTE — Sprayers with cone angles less than 90° and 
K-factors less than 26 are permissible for local protection such 
as protuberances. For product piping, it is permissible to use 
wide-angled sprayers, than 125°. 


8.5.1.6 Minimum and maximum pressures in the 
network shall be 1.4 bar and 3.5 bar, respectively. 


8.5.1.7 ‘Run down’, shall not be considered. 


8.5.1.8 Sprayers shall be normal to the exposed 
surface of the sphere and shall be installed at not less 
than 550 mm or more than 650 mm from the surface. 


8.5.1.9 Spheres shall be spaced at a distance of 
minimum 15 m from each other. In such cases the water 
demand for a larger sphere shall determine the pumping 
and storage requirements. If the spheres are spaced 
less than 15 m apart, the aggregate water demand of 
all the spheres falling within the prescribed distance of 
each other shall be the determining factor for hydraulic 
calculations. 


8.5.2 System Design 
8.5.2.1 Density of discharge 


Water shall be applied at a minimum density of 
10.2 Ipm/m? of the exposed area of the sphere. The 
supporting legs and the product pipes within the bund 
area shall also receive water at the same density. Where 
bund is not provided, the product pipelines up to a 
distance of 15 m from the surface of the sphere shall 
receive water at the same density. 


NOTES 
1 If the supporting legs are encased with 50 mm thick RCC, the 
water density, therefore, can be reduced to 5.1 Ipm/m?. 


2 Selection of sprayers and pipe sizes shall be in such a way 
as to avoid overspray on the sphere surface and the achieved 
density should be preferably within 20 percent of the design 
density as above. 


8.5.2.2 Distribution of sprayers and layout of piping 
The following considerations shall be made: 


a) No sprayer shall be farther than the distance ‘S’ 
indicated in Fig. 10, from anyone of the nearest 
8 sprayers. The distance between sprayers shall 
be measured along the arcs between the points 
of impingement of the sprayers on the tank 
surface. 


b) The spacing ‘S’ between the sprayers for various 
diameters of the sphere for different cone angles of 


IS 15325 : 2020 


c 


d 


e 


8 


wa 


wa 


wa 


a 


Fic. 10 SPACING OF SPRAYERS 


sprayers shall be selected based on the following 
parameters: 


1) Manufacturer’s recommendation and the spray 
pattern provided by them. 


2) Total exposed surface area of the sphere 
shall be impinged without any possibility of 
hotspots. 


3) The spray pattern shall overlap on the surface 
of the sphere by at least 5 percent. 


Obstructed or ‘roofed off’ portions of the spheres 
shall be protected with separate sprayers in 
addition to the requirements under 8.5.2.2 (b) 
above at a density of 10.2 lpm/m’. 


Number of horizontal and/or vertical rings shall 
be governed by the spacing of the sprayers 
[see 8.5.2.2(b)]. 


The system shall be hydraulically designed in such 
a way that the pressure at the hydraulically most 
unfavourable sprayer shall not be less than 1.4 bar 
while that at the hydraulically most favourable 
sprayer shall not exceed 3.5 bar. The difference in 
height between the top and bottom sprayers may 
be compensated for by reducing sprayer office 
and/or other means to achieve even distribution of 
water on the surface. The velocity produced in the 
feeder pipes shall not exceed 10 m/s. 


Cooling system for protecting the sphere against 
solar heating shall take the form of minimum two 
rings of sprayers at the top of the spheres upto 
10 m diameter and three rings of sprayers at the 
top of the sphere exceeding 10 m diameter at a 
density not less than 2 Ipm/m/?. 
NOTE — It is not considered necessary to wet the surface of 
the sphere below the horizontal centre line when considering 
solar protection. 
Spacing of sprayers for the product pipelines shall 
not exceed 3 m and sprayers shall be at a distance 
of not more than 800 mm from the pipes (see 
also 8.5.1.5). 


22 


8.5.3 Pipe Support 


8.5.3.1 The pipe work on the top of hemisphere of the 
vessel shall rest on the surface and an adequate number 
of support points shall be required to distribute the 
weight uniformly on the surface. 


8.5.3.2 The pipe work below the hemisphere shall 
be supported separately from the ground or the legs 
supporting the sphere. The legs shall be designed to 
take care of this load. 


8.5.3.3 Where supports rest on the surface of the 
sphere, synthetic elastomer insertion shall be provided 
beneath the base of the support and the sphere surface 
to accommodate the curvature of the sphere as well as 
to prevent corrosion. 


8.5.3.4 Where the vessel is insulated, supports shall 
have to either penetrate the lagging or provided on the 
lagging itself. In either case, greater care shall have to 
be taken to adequately spread the load and efficiently 
seal the penetrated area of the lagging after supports 
are installed. 


8.5.4 Detection System 


8.5.4.1 It is not necessary to provide detector sprinklers 
for the whole surface of the sphere. Detectors at three 
levels shall suffice as follows: 


a) Aminimum of three under the lower pole adjacent 
to product piping. 

b) A ring of detectors at the equator or just below. 
The detectors shall be installed at not more than 
2.5 m of the circumference of sphere. 


c) Aminimum of three detectors at the upper crown 
of the sphere in the advantageous position near 
relief valves, vents, etc. 


d) All protuberances on the sphere shall be separately 
provided with individual detectors. 


8.5.4.2 The detector shall be suitably supported, if 
required on sprayer piping. 


8.5.4.3 The detector shall, in any case, be installed at 
not more than 300 mm from the surface protected. 


8.5.4.4 Detectors shall also be installed near the product 
pipes at every 2.5 m and at least up to 15 m from the 
shell surface of the sphere. 


8.5.5 Pumping Capacity 


The aggregate pumping capacity shall be determined by 
the largest demand arising out of one or more of deluge 
valves when vessels concerned operate simultaneously 
[see 11.1 (c) and Table 9]. 


8.5.6 Water Supply 
See 11. 


8.6 Tunnels, Cable Galleries and Cable Cellars 
8.6.1 General 


8.6.1.1 Where cable fires are concerned, the greatest 
hazard usually arises from the effects of fire on the 
power station plant. However, a feature of practically 
all cable fires has been that several units, if not the 
whole station, has been seriously affected by a single 
fire. A major portion of cable fire incidents stem from 
external sources such as combustion of un-cleaned 
flammable debris, accumulation of PVC tailing ends, 
cardboard packages and from uncontrolled spillages, 
over spray of fuel and lubricating oils. 


8.6.1.2 PVC is not readily flammable but will burn 
freely in temperature conditions high enough to 
bring the plasticisers into a volatile state. Burning 
PVC produces copious quantities of dangerous 
hydrochloride toxic gases, which are heavier than air 
and tend to form layers at lower levels. These gases are 
corrosive and present a major toxic hazard to operating 
and firefighting personnel. When PVC is burnt, heavy 
black smoke, mostly consisting of carbon particles, 
is given off which could affect electrical equipment 
some distance from the fire and there is some evidence 
that PVC smoke can de-sensitise smoke detectors of 
ionisation chamber type. 


8.6.1.3 Cables are normally protected such that they 
do not catch fire if electrical faults develop in them. 
However, the energy released when a fault occurs in 
a cable may ignite other combustible materials in the 
vicinity thereof. 


8.6.2 Design Density 


Water shall be applied at a minimum density 
of 10.2 Ipm/m? of the exposed area of the cable racks. 


NOTE — For the purpose of the above, three cable trays of a 
rack shall be reckoned as a single tray unless the trays are not 
of the same width in which case the area of the widest tray shall 
be taken (see also 8.6.4.5 ). 


23 


IS 15325 : 2020 


8.6.3 Pressure Requirement 


In order to achieve a better penetration, a minimum 
pressure of 2.1 bar shall be achieved at the hydraulically 
remotest point. 


8.6.4 Distribution of Sprayers and Layout of Piping 


8.6.4.1 The sprayers shall be installed in rows at ceiling 
level in between and at the centre of aisle space along 
the cable trays and spaced at not more than 3 m. 


8.6.4.2 The distance between walls and/or limits of the 
protection shall not exceed 1.5 m. 


8.6.4.3 Where the distance between two rows of 
sprayers above the aisles exceeds 4 m, additional row 
of sprayers shall be provided (see 8.6.4.1). 


8.6.4.4 Where the height of the cable trays (that is, 
distance between topmost and bottom tray) exceeds 
2.5 m, sprayers shall be provided below the lowest 
tray. 


8.6.4.5 When the cable racks contain more than three 
trays, system protection shall be designed as follows 
(see also 8.6.2): 


a) Protection shall be extended to cover every three 
trays (below the top three) or part thereof by 
dropping pipes from the sprayer network at roof 
level. 


b) Sprayers shall be so installed that their pattern 
covers all the three trays and water can penetrate 
inside to provide adequate protection to the cables. 


c) Sprayers shall be spaced at a minimum of 2.5 m 
along the longitudinal side of the cable racks. 


d) Sprayers and the piping shall be suitably supported 
to avoid oscillation and protected against possible 
mechanical damage. 


8.6.5 System Hydraulics 


8.6.5.1 Installation of piping shall be carried out, in 
general, as detailed in 9.3 to 9.7. 


8.6.5.2 It is permissible to divide the protection area 
into several zones, each of which shall be fed by an 
individual deluge valve. Each zone shall not exceed 
30 m length. The flow through the deluge valve shall 
be limited to the values in Table 7. The system shall 
be designed in such a way that at least two zones shall 
operate simultaneously in the event of fire. 


8.6.5.3 Each zone in the system shall be hydraulically so 
designed that a minimum pressure of 2.1 bar is available 
at the remotest sprayer and maximum pressure in the 
installation shall not exceed 3.5 bar. Velocity produced 
in the feeder pipes shall not be more than 10 m/s. 


8.6.5.4 Detailed hydraulic calculations along with nodal 
drawings in support of the above shall be submitted for 
each zone. Orifice plates, if required, shall arise out of 


IS 15325 : 2020 


combination of deluge valves when zones concerned 
operate simultaneously. 


8.6.6 Detection System 


8.6.6.1 As the cable galleries and tunnels are normally 
unmanned, it is imperative that a quicker detection is 
mandatory to ensure extinguishment. Various types of 
detectors are available for installation in the tunnels. 
The following methods of detection in the order 
mentioned are generally accepted. The installation 
shall comply with various provisions of IS 2189 and 
IS 15105, where applicable: 


a) Linear heat sensing cables; 


b) Smoke detectors; and 
c) Sprinkler heads. 


8.6.6.2 Full details of the proposal shall be submitted 
to the authorities concerned in advance along with 
detailed drawings showing the location and layout of 
the detection network. 


8.6.6.3 The fire alarm system and panel shall be of 
approved type and in compliance with IS 2189 and 
IS 15908, where applicable. 


8.6.6.4 Authorities concerned can accept other types 
of detectors, which may be subject to verification of 
the proposals submitted in advance. 


8.6.7 Pumping Capacity 


The aggregate pumping capacity shall be determined by 
the largest demand arising out of combination of deluge 
valves when zones concerned operate simultaneously. 


8.6.8 Water Supply 
See 11. 


8.7 Conveyors 
8.7.1 General 


8.7.1.1 Fires on conveyors are infrequent but the fire 
potential is considerable. In incidents which have 
occurred, the damage has been severe, particularly 
where conveyor fires have reached and enveloped the 
destination for example, boiler house, coal bunkers 
as in case of thermal power stations. The design of 
conveyors is that the wind tubular or chimney effect 
is an inherent feature on inclined conveyors and this 
causes rapid spread of fire through the conveyors. 


8.7.1.2 The major risk of fire is for example, from the 
ignition of coal dust and deposits in case of thermal 
power stations, on the internal surface, walkways, etc, 
of the conveyors or from the conveyor belt. Fire caused 
by friction of a defective part such as jammed roller, 
idlers resulting in subsequent localised overheating of 
the belt. Thus fires in the conveyors may arise from 


24 


either of two main causes: 


a) Failure of part of the mechanism, usually on the 
idler or pulley can lead to localised overheating 
of the belt and eventually to ignition of the 
combustible dust or conveyor belt; and 


b) From the ignition ofa quantity of split combustible 
dust either by self-ignition or other causes. 


8.7.1.3 Should the belt catch fire, it can spread the fire 
rapidly to other areas. Certain fires generate a large 
volume of smoke, particularly when the fire is in an 
advanced state conveyors can be protected by automatic 
sprinkler system installation or medium velocity water 
spray system with linear heat sensing (LHS) cables, 
sprinkler bulbs, thermocouples, etc, and the following 
provisions cover requirements for water spray system 
only. 


8.7.2 Design Density 


Water shall be applied at a minimum density of 
10.2 Ipm/m? of the exposed area of the conveyor. 


8.7.3 Pressure Requirement 


A minimum pressure of 1.4 bar shall be achieved at 
the hydraulically remote sprayer. However, pressure at 
the hydraulically favourable sprayer shall not exceed 
3.5 bar. 


8.7.4 Distribution of Sprayers and Layout of Piping 


8.7.4.1 The sprayers shall be installed in rows at the 
ceiling level above the centre of each conveyor belt and 
spaced at not more than 4 m. 


8.7.4.2 The distance between walls and/or limits of the 
protection shall not exceed 2 m. 


8.7.4.3 Where the distance between two rows of sprayers 
above the centre of belts exceeds 4 m, additional rows 
shall be provided. 


8.7.4.4 Sprayers shall be provided for the protection 
of the bottom side of the conveyors and these shall be 
spaced at 4 m on either side of the conveyor. Staggering 
of sprayers is recommended. 


8.7.4.5 Area covered by each sprayer shall not be more 
than 12 m? or less than 9 m?’. 


8.7.5 System Hydraulics 


8.7.5.1 Installation of piping shall be carried out in 
general as detailed in 9.3 to 9.7. 


8.7.5.2 It is permissible to divide the protection area 
into several zones, each of which shall be fed by an 
individual deluge valve. The flow through the deluge 
valve shall be limited to those given in Table 7. The 
system shall be designed in such a way that at least two 
adjacent zones shall operate in the event of fire. 


8.7.5.3 Each zone in the system shall be hydraulically 
so designed that a minimum pressure of 1.4 bar is 
available at the remotest sprayer and that nowhere in 
the system exceeds 3.5 bar. The velocity produced shall 
not exceed 10 m/s. 


8.7.5.4 Detailed hydraulic calculations along with nodal 
drawings in support of the above shall be prepared for 
each zone. Orifice plates, if required, shall arise out of 
combination of deluge valves when zones concerned 
operate simultaneously. 


8.7.6 Pumping Capacity 


The aggregate pumping capacity shall be determined by 
the largest demand arising out of combination of deluge 
valves when zones concerned operate simultaneously. 


8.7.7 Water Supply 
See 11. 


8.7.8 Detection System 


8.7.8.1 Detection of conveyor fires poses peculiar 
problems as the fires are not always stationary. 
Detection of moving fires shall be achieved without 
delay. The detectors upon sensing the fire shall trip the 
conveyor motor first and thus make the fire stationary. 
This fire has to be detected and the detectors shall 
trigger the firefighting operations. Hence, there 
are two levels of detection for the conveyor fires. 
The following methods of detection are generally 
acceptable: 


a) Liner heat sensing cables for stopping conveyor, 
and 


b) Sprinkler bulbs. 


8.7.8.2 Full details of the protection shall be submitted 
to authorities concerned in advance along with detailed 
drawings showing the location and layout of the 
detection network. 


8.7.8.3 The fire alarm system and panel shall be 
of approved type in accordance with IS 2189 and 
IS 15105, where applicable. 


8.7.8.4 Authorities concerned reserve their right in 
accepting other types of detectors, which is subject to 
verification of the proposals well in advance.

or in masonry culverts with removable covers of

9.1.3 The pipe used in the spray system (from the pump 
house to the deluge valves) can also be laid above 
ground in case of piping materials as per 9.1.2 with 
welded [except in case of 9.1.2(c)], threaded or flanged 
or grooved joints subject to following conditions: 


a) Pipes shall be laid in exclusive steel supports and 
shall not run in pipe racks with other utility piping. 


IS 15325 : 2020 


b) The pipes shall be run at minimum distances as 
stated below: 


1) Light hazard 
2) Ordinary hazard 
3) High hazard (including open storage) : 15 m 


:6m 


:6m 


9.1.4 Pipes shall not be laid under buildings or plant 
areas or storage areas. As far as possible, pipes shall not 
be laid under large open storage, railroads and roads 
carrying heavy traffic. 


9.1.5 Underground pipes shall be laid not less than 1 m 
below ground level. Pipes running under roads shall 
be routed through home pipes to avoid damage to the 
pipes due to traffic and vehicle movement. 


9.1.6 Underground pipes in case of materials in 9.1.1 
shall be provided with masonry or equivalent supports 
and thrust blocks (where necessary) at regular intervals. 


9.1.7 Where soil conditions are unsatisfactory, masonry 
or equivalent supports shall be provided at regular 
intervals for all other pipes also. 


9.1.8 Pipes shall not traverse on ground, which is not 
under the control of the owner of the installation. Pipes 
shall also not pass through public roadways. 


9.1.9 The installation piping (from the pump house 
upto deluge valve and also the installation piping with 
sprayers above the deluge valve) shall be capable of 
withstanding for 2 ha pressure equivalent to 150 percent 
of the maximum working pressure. 


9.1.10 All bolt holes in the flanges shall be drilled. 
Drilling of each flange shall be in accordance with the 
relevant Indian standards. 


9.1.11 Flanges shall be faced and have jointing of 
rubber insertions or asbestos compound. 


9.1.12 Welded joints of any type shall not be permitted 
for pipes having diameter less than 50 mm. 


9.1.13 It is not permissible to run the spray system 
pipes through a building or occupancy (not protected 
by sprinkler or spray systems) and where it is not 
practicable, the supply pipeline shall be installed at 
ground level and enclosed in brick trenches covered 
with removable RCC precast slabs. 


9.1.14 All installation pipework above ground shall be 
installed at a slope not less than 1 : 500 for horizontal 
run of pipes. Normally the pipework should slope 
through the deluge valve. If the pipework is trapped 
(below the level of the deluge valve for example, in 
the basements), arrangements shall be made to provide 
drain cocks at the bottom of such pipes to drain the 
trapped water. 


26 


9.1.15 Sprayer pipes shall not be embedded in concrete 
floors or ceilings of any building. 


9.2 Fittings 


9.2.1 Fittings installed underground shall be of cast 
iron heavy grade conforming to IS 1538 whereas 
those installed over ground shall be of medium grade 
wrought or mild steel conforming to IS 1239 (Part 2) 
or malleable iron fittings conforming to IS 1879 or 
IS 9523 for ductile iron fittings. 


9.2.2 All fittings shall be able to withstand at least a 
pressure of 150 percent of the maximum working 
pressure. 


9.2.3 Welded fittings according to the laid down 
welding procedure are permitted. Welded parts shall be 
galvanized or suitably coated after welding as per the 
requirement of the areas to be protected by the system 
that is, chemical and electrolytic corrosion. 


9.2.4 Welded joints shall not be permitted for fittings of 
less than 50 mm diameter. 


9.2.5 Grooved couplings including their gaskets used 
in water spray systems shall be approved for use in dry 
systems. 


9.3 Joining of Piping and Fittings 


9.3.1 Threaded Pipes and Fittings 


a) All threaded pipes and fittings shall have threads 
cut as per relevant Indian Standards. 


b) Steel pipes with thicknesses less than schedule 
30 (size 200 mm or more) and those of schedule 
40 (size less than 200 mm) shall be permitted to be 
jointed only with threaded fittings. 


c) Joint compound or tape shall be applied only to 
male threads. 


9.3.2 Welded Pipe and Fittings 


Pipes meant for spray installation shall only be shop 
welded, unless permitted by the authorities or agencies 
responsible for approval of the spray system. Welding 
shall be done under supervision as per proper approved 
procedures through qualified welders. Necessary 
records shall be maintained with regard to work 
completed, defects observed, re-work and clearance, 
etc. Also details of radiography test for the welded 
pipes duly signed by the protocol shall be maintained. 


9.3.3 Groove Joining Methods 


Pipes joined with grooved couplings shall be joined by 
approved couplings, gaskets and groove dimensions. 
Grooved connections of fittings and valves and 
grooves cut and rolled on pipe shall be dimensionally 
compatible with the couplings. 


9.4 Pipe Supporting Methods (Above Deluge Valve) 


9.4.1 General (Building or General Area Protection) 


Sprayer pipes shall be supported from the building 
structure which, itself shall be capable of supporting 
the water filled pipework and shall not impair the 
performance of sprayers under fire conditions. Pipework 
shall not be used to support any other loads except 
where primary support is designed for the suspension 
of the piped service. Distribution/range pipes shall not 
be supported from ceiling sheathing or cladding or 
from any other associated suspension systems. Pipes 
below obstructions, such as, ductwork shall be either 
supported from the building structure or from the steel 
members supporting such obstructions. Such members 
shall be capable of supporting the weight of water filled 
pipes too. 


Hangers shall not be welded or fastened directly to the 
pipework. The supports on which the pipework rests 
shall be secured firmly in position. The thickness of 
all parts of pipe supports shall not be less than 3 mm. 
Wherever possible, pipes shall be supported from non- 
combustible building elements. Pipework in corrosive 
areas shall be of either stainless steel or suitably 
protected against corrosion. The distance between the 
pipe supports measured along the line of connected 
pipes (whether the pipes run horizontally, vertically or 
at angles) shall not be less than that given in Table 6. 


Table 6 Distance Between Pipe Supports 
( Clause 9.4.1) 


SI No. Pipe Diameter Spacing 
mm m 
(1) (2) (3) 
i) Up to 65 4 
ii) More than 65 and up to 100 6 
iii) More than 100 and up to 250 6.5 


9.4.2 Distribution Pipes 


The first support on a nominally horizontal distribution 
pipe shall not be at more than 2 m from the main 
distribution pipe. The last support on a nominally 
horizontal distribution pipe shall not be more than 
450 mm from the end. Drop or rise pipes shall be 
secured to the building structure either directly or 
indirectly at the adjacent nominally horizontal part of 
the pipe within 300 mm of the drop or rise. 


27 


IS 15325 : 2020 


9.4.3 Range Pipes 
At least one support shall be provided for: 
a) each pipe run connecting adjacent sprinkler, and 


b) the pipe run connecting the distribution pipe and 
the first sprinkler on the range pipe. 


9.4.3.1 Pipe supports shall not be closer than 150 mm 
to any sprinkler axial central line. The first support 
on a range pipe shall not be more than 2 m from the 
distribution pipe. The last support on a range pipe shall 
not be located more than 1.5 m from, 


a) the range pipe end; 


b) where there is a horizontal arm pipe of 450 mm or 
longer, the arm pipe end; or 


c) where there is a drop or rise exceeding 600 mm, 
the drop or rise pipe end. 


9.4.4 Outgoing mains from the installation valve to the 
system shall be supported at every 3.5 m of its run. 


9.4.5 The thickness of all components used in pipe 
supports shall not be less than 3 mm anywhere. 


9.4.6 Some of the typical supporting arrangements are 
shown in Fig. 11. 


9.5 Protection against Fire and Mechanical Damages 


Piping shall be installed in such a way that the pipes 
are not exposed to mechanical damage. Where pipes 
are installed above gangways with low headroom or 
at intermediate levels or in other similar situations, 
precautions shall be taken against mechanical damage. 


Where it is unavoidable for water supply pipework to 
pass through a building or occupancy (not protected 
by sprinkler or spray systems), it shall be installed at 
ground level and shall be enclosed to protect against 
mechanical damage, with appropriate fire resistance. 


9.6 Painting 


Non-galvanized ferrous pipework shall be painted if 
environmental conditions make itnecessary. Galvanized 
piping shall be painted wherever the coating has been 
damaged for example, by threading. 


9.7 Drainage (Pipelines) 


Means shall be provided to enable all the pipework to 
be drained. Where this cannot be done through the drain 
valve at the deluge valve, extra valves shall be fitted 
as specified in 9.9.3. Range pipes shall have a slope 
towards the distribution pipe of at least 0.4 percent 
and distribution pipes shall have a slope towards the 
appropriate drain valve of at least 0.2 percent. Range

9.8 Valves 
9.8.1 General 


The various types of valves used in the installation are 
stop valves, drain valves, and deluge valves. All stop 
valves which may cut off water supply to the sprinkler 
installation shall, 


a) close in the clockwise direction; 


b) be fitted with an indicator that clearly shows 
whether it is in the open or closed position; and 


c) be secured in the right position by a strap and 
padlock or secured in an equivalent manner. 


Butterfly valves, if used, shall be of the gear operated 
type for sizes more than 150 mm and motor operated 
if more than 300 mm (see IS 13095). Valves which 
interlock when closed shall be positioned in a 
conspicuous place where the key is obtrusive when the 
valve is closed. 


9.8.2 Main Stop Valves 


Where spray systems are fed by a ring main supply 
pipe arrangement on the premises stop valves shall be 
installed to isolate the ring into sections in such a way 
that no section shall include more than 3 deluge valves. 
The main stop valve(s) shall be at a fire brigade access 
level and readily accessible when responding to a fire 
alarm. Where the working pressure of the installation is 
more than 7 kg/cm? cast iron valves with PN 1.6 rating 
(nominal pressure) shall be provided. However, cast 
steel valves of class 150 shall suffice for installation 
under all pressure conditions. 


9.8.3 Drain Valves 


Drain valves sized as below shall be fitted to allow 
drainage from: 


a) Immediately downstream of the installation alarm 
valve or, if fitted, its downstream stop valve; 

b) Immediately downstream of any stop valve; 

c) Any pipe other than drop pipes to single sprayers 
which cannot be drained through another drain 
valve; 


d 


wn 


Valves shall be fitted at the lower end of permanent 
pipework. The outlet shall be not more than 3 m 
above the floor and shall be fitted with a brass 
plug; and 

e) Where it is not possible to drain the water from 
a distribution or range pipe, drain pipes shall be 
provided as stated below: 


1) Trapped distribution pipes : 40 mm 


2) Trapped range pipes :25 mm 


29 


IS 15325 : 2020 


9.9 Deluge Valves 


9.9.1 A deluge system is a fixed fire protection system 
which totally floods an area with pressurized water 
through a system of piping with open nozzles and/ 
or sprinklers. The system piping is empty until the 
controlling valve is activated by pneumatic or other 
types of release systems. Such controlling valves 
which are quick opening in nature are called ‘deluge 
valves’. The deluge valve assembly consists mainly of 
the following: 


a) In line strainer; 
b) Isolation valve; 
c) Deluge valve; 
d) Drain valve; 


e) Pressure gauges (above and below the deluge 
valve); 


f) Alarm assembly (consisting of gong or sounder); 
and 


g) Actuator/pilot assembly. 


9.9.2 Varieties of deluge valves with different working 
principles are available and hence it is necessary that the 
valves shall have approval from national/international 
approving bodies. 


9.9.3 Principle of Operation 


The deluge valve has an inlet, outlet and priming 
chamber. The inlet and outlet are separated from the 
priming chamber by the valve chamber and diaphragm. 
In the ‘SET’ position, pressure is applied to the priming 
chamber through a restricted prime line. The pressure is 
trapped in the priming chamber and holds the clapper/ 
diaphragm on the seat due to the differential design. In 
the set position, the clapper/diaphragm separates the 
inlet from the outlet keeping the system piping dry. 
When the pressure is released from priming chamber 
faster than it is supplied through the restricted priming 
line, the clapper moves and allows the inlet water 
supply to flow through the outlet into the system and 
associated alarm device. 


The mode of actuation of deluge valve can be pneumatic 
or hydraulic type or a combination of both. 


9.9.4 Requirements of Installation 


The following lists the necessary requirements to 
ensure proper installation: 


a) Deluge valve shall be installed outside of but 
adjacent to the protected area as close to the risk 
as possible but at not less than 6 m from the plant 
and/or equipment to be protected. 


b) Masonry enclosures shall be provided around 
the deluge valve in the form of barrier walls in 
such a way that the valve is not exposed to any 


IS 15325 : 2020 


impact due to flying bodies or projectiles from the 
plant and/or equipment in the vicinity and also for 
weather protection. 


c) Isolating valves shall be provided below the 
deluge valves to enable servicing thereof and 
cleaning strainers at regular intervals. 


d) Isolating valves shall be provided above the 
deluge valve in addition, for testing purposes. 


e) The isolating valves shall be strapped and locked 
in open position by leather straps or nylon chains 
and pad locks under normal operating condition. 


f) Emergency manual override facility shall be 
provided for actuating the deluge valve. 


g) It is permissible to provide a manually operated 
bypass line with an isolating valve for emergency 
requirements. Such valves shall always be kept 
locked in closed position. 


h) The load on the deluge valve shall not exceed the 
limits mentioned in Table 7. 

j) Indicators shall be provided to show the open and 
closed positions. 

k) Facility shall be provided to prime the space above 
the deluge valve seat with water. 

m) It must be ensured that there is no possibility of 
water leaking back into the instrument air supply 
in the event of diaphragm failure. 


n 


wm 


A suitable, durable, robust and clearly visible 
instruction plate shall be permanently secured 
to each assembly and shall detail clearly and 
concisely the following procedures: 


1) Start up (or operation), 
2) Test, 

3) Shut down, or 

4) Drain. 


9.9.5 Deluge valve shall not be subject to a working 
pressure of more than 12 bar.

9.10 Drainage Provisions (Protection Areas) 


Adequate provisions shall be made to promptly and 
effectively dispose of all liquids from the fire area 
during operation of all systems in the fire area. Such 
provision shall be adequate for, 


a) water discharged from fixed fire protection 
systems at maximum flow conditions; 


b) water likely to be discharged by hose streams; 
c) surface water; and 
d) cooling water normally discharged to the systems. 


9.10.1 There are four methods generally adopted for 
disposal and/or containment that is, grading, dyking, 
trenching, underground or enclosed drain systems. 


The method used in drainage shall be governed by, 
a) the extent of the hazard; 
b) clear space available; and 
c) the protection required. 


Where the hazard is low, the clear space is adequate 
and degree of protection required is not great, grading 
is acceptable. Where these conditions are not present, 
consideration shall be given to dykes, trenches or 
underground or enclosed drains. Where grading is 
employed, a slope of not less than 1 percent shall be 
necessary. Concrete surfacing is mostly desirable, 
however, other hard surfacing are acceptable 


Where dyking is employed, the drainage arrangements 
thereof shall conform to Indian Petroleum Rules in all 
respects. Where trenching, underground or enclosed 
drains are employed necessary approval of the 
Authority may be taken. 


9.11 Alarms and Alarm Devices 


Each deluge valve set shall be provided with a water 
motor alarm suitable for spray service located as close 
as possible to the deluge valve. Electrically operated 
alarm shall also be accepted. Alarm gong shall go into 
operation within a maximum of 90 s of opening of 
deluge valve. Water motor alarm gong shall comply 
with various provisions of IS 15105. 


Each water motor/electric alarm gong shall be 
prominently marked with the number of the installation 
to indicate the building/area protected by the deluge 
valve. The water motor shall be installed with its gong 
on the outside of an exterior wall and with its centre 
line not higher than 6 m above the point of connection 
to the deluge valve. A strainer, readily accessible for 
cleaning, shall be fitted between the motor nozzle and 
the deluge valve connection. The water outlet shall be 
positioned so that any flow of water can be seen. 


The pipework to the water motor alarm gong shall 
be galvanized, medium grade steel complying with 
IS 1239 (Parts 1 and 2). The equivalent length of pipe 


between the deluge valve and the water motor shall 
be not more than 20 m assuming an equivalent length 
of 3 m for each change of direction. The nominal size 
shall be not less than, 


a) 15 mm for equivalent lengths less than or equal to 
6 m; and 


b) 20 mm for equivalent lengths greater than 6 m. 


Any device to reduce the frequency of false or 
intermittent alarms fitted to the spray installation shall 
be suitable for spray system service. 


9.12 Pressure Gauges 


9.12.1 General and Specification 


Pressure gauges fitted in the installations shall comply 
with relevant Indian Standards. 


The scale subdivision shall not exceed: 


a) 0.2 bar for a maximum scale value upto and 
including 10 bar. 


b) 0.5 bar for a maximum scale value of more than 
10 bar, up to and including 16 bar. 


The maximum scale value shall be twice the maximum 
pressure. 


9.12.2 Application of Pressure Gauges 


a) Deluge valves — A pressure gauge shall be fitted 
at each of the following points: 


1) Main control valve, 


2) Immediately downstream of the deluge valve 
(designated the ‘C’ gauge), and 


3) Immediately upstream of the main control stop 
valve (designated the ‘B’ gauge). 


b) Water supply connections — Each pump supply 
shall be fitted with a damped pressure gauge on 
the supply pipe immediately downstream of the 
outlet check valve and upstream of any outlet stop 
valve. 


c) Removal — Means shall be provided to enable 
each pressure gauge to be removed readily 
without interruption of the water or air supply to 
the installation. 


9.13 Pressure Regulating Valves (PRVs) 


Pressure regulating valves shall be used to restrict 
unwarranted pressure in the installation and piping, 
particularly in high rise installations. In any case, PRVs 
shall be provided where the system pressure is in excess 
of 12 bar. Pressure gauges shall be provided on the inlet 
and outlet sides of each PRV. A relief valve shall be 
provided of size not less than 15 mm on the discharge 
side of the PRVs so as to relieve excess pressure. Means 
shall be provided downstream of all PRVs for flow tests 
at spray system demand. 


31 


IS 15325 : 2020 


9.14 Strainers 


Main pipe line strainers shall be provided for spray 
systems utilizing nozzles and projectors with waterways 
less than 10 mm and for any system where the water 
is likely to contain obstructive material. Main pipeline 
strainers shall be so installed as to be easily accessible 
for flushing and cleaning. 


Individual or integral strainers shall be provided at each 
nozzle/projector where waterways smaller than 5 mm 
are used. Strainers shall be capable of removing from 
the water all solids of sufficient size to prevent the spray 
nozzles from clogging (normally 3 mm perforations 
are suitable). Strainers shall be normally located just 
upstream of the system deluge valve and shall be 
downstream thereof, if any. Strainers shall be capable 
of allowing continued operation, without seriously 
increasing the head loss, for a period estimated to be 
ample considering the type of protection provided, the 
condition of the water, and other local circumstances. 


In some cases, a bypass may be warranted to facilitate 
periodic cleaning of the strainer at intervals based on 
water quality and strainer obstruction experience. 


9.15 Detection System 


Detection systems are designed to detect one or more 
of three characteristics of a fire that is, smoke, heat 
and radiation. No one type of detector is most suitable 
for all applications and final choice will depend on 
individual circumstances. 


In any automatic fire detection system, a detector 
has to discriminate between a fire and the normal 
environmental conditions. The overall objective of 
the system is intended not only to enable a fire to be 
detected at an early stage of its occurrence but also 
to extinguish the fire without extensive property 
damage. 


Water spray systems (manual or automatic) shall 
be provided with an audible alarm at the protected 
premises to indicate that the system has been actuated. 
When a water spray system is in a remote area, a 
system for monitoring the alarm should be in place. 
This monitoring should be at an attended location such 
as a control room. 


Systems shall be automatic for all types of application 
except certain areas where application is localized or 
where an efficient detection system cannot be provided. 
Nevertheless, automatic actuation is still considered a 
preferred approach for remote or unstaffed locations 
needing fire protection. IS 2189 shall be referred for 
additional installation requirements for detection 
systems that are intended to operate water spray 
systems. 


Automatically operated systems can help minimize 
damage by providing faster operation of the system as 


IS 15325 : 2020 


well as provide an alarm for quicker action by facility 
personnel. Automatic detection can be accomplished 
by the use of fire and/or gas detection systems installed 
within the protected area. Fire detection can include all 
types of electronic or pneumatic systems (discussed 
in detail in IS 2189), or may use a fixed temperature 
sprinkler system in accordance with provisions of this 
standard. 


In case of water spray systems, detection systems 
are required for activating the deluge system for the 
following applications: 


a) General area protection (indoors); 

b) Horizontal and vertical vessels (outdoors); 
c) Spherical vessels (outdoors); 

d) Transformers (outdoors and indoors); 


e) Spot protection such as oil tanks, turbo-alternator 
sets, pipe lines, etc (outdoors and indoors); 


f) Cable galleries; and 
g) Conveyors. 


For most of the above protections, sprinklers are found 
in extensive application in view of their suitability. 


Sprinklers are not fast enough for certain applications, 
for example, general areas like, open-sided bottling 
plants for LPG and the like, open-sided chemical plants 
handling low flashing solvents, etc, where a quick 
detection is required to avoid an inferno. 


Other types of detectors, such as flame detectors (either 
infrared or ultra violet types or combination of both), 
gas detectors, video detectors, etc, are options for much 
quicker detection and in this regard, provisions in 
IS 2189 shall be complied with for installation of such 
detection systems. 


The design of detection system by sprinklers varies 
from application to application in case of water spray 
systems. Hence all the methods have been separately 
covered under each section. However, following 
requirements are common to all types of application 
and these requirements are listed below: 


1) Sprinkler piping shall not be less than 25 mm 
diameter anywhere; 


2) Total pipeline volume shall not be less than 
10 1 (0.01 m°); 


3) Pressure in the detection system shall, in no case, 
exceed 3.5 bar; 


4) Detection piping shall slope to drain at least 1 in 
250 with drain valves provided at the lowest point; 
and 


5) For pneumatic, separate air compressor shall 
be provided for the detection system. The air 
compressor shall be installed in the fire pump 
room. Where it is not possible, the air compressor 


32 


room shall be separated from the occupancies 
adjoining therewith as per 10.3(c). 
6) Wherever possible, in case of pneumatic systems, 
standby air compressor may be installed or 
supplies from process and utility compressors 
may be connected as an alternate supply to the 
detection system. 


7 


x 


As far as possible, the detection piping shall be run 
alongside the underground spray mains but run 
independently of other pipes, either underground 
or aboveground. The piping shall be suitably 
protected against impact damage in the case of the 
latter. 


8 


wa 


Detection piping shall not traverse underneath or 
through any working/storage blocks or tank farms/ 
materials stored in open. 


9) Temperature rating of the detector sprinkler 
shall be at least 30°C above the highest ambient 
temperature at the site of installation. 


10) Detection piping and equipment installed in 
corrosive areas shall be applied with protective 
coatings. 


11) Detection piping and equipment shall be supported 
independently as far as possible. 


12) Detection piping/equipment shall be laid away 
from hot sources, such as heat exchangers, 
furnaces, ovens, etc in order to avoid possible 
false alarms. 


13) Sprinkler heads shall be provided with guards in 
areas where they are susceptible to mechanical 
damage and care shall be taken to see that the 
guards do not interfere with the spray pattern in 
the vicinity. 


14 


NS 


Detection system shall be designed to cause 
actuation of the deluge valve within 20 s under 
expected exposure conditions. 


15) It is recommended to provide baffle plates for 
detectors where situation warrants.

10.1 Pumping Capacity Requirement 


a) To determine the actual pumping capacity required 
for the system, individual demands of various 
detached buildings/equipment within the complex 
shall be determined based on the design details 
given in the previous sections.

wm 


The pumping capacity required shall be equivalent 
to the highest of the demands thus calculated in (a) 
above. 


c) Suitable pump shall then be selected to match with 
the duty parameters as shown in Table 8. 


10.2 General Requirements 


The following requirements are applicable: 


a) 


Pump sets shall be exclusively used for the spray 
systems and shall be of an approved type and shall 
be one of the following types: 


1) Electric motor driven centrifugal pumps; 


2) Compression ignition engine driven centrifugal 
pumps; and 
3) Vertical turbine submersible pumps. 


In all the above cases, pumps shall be automatic in 
action. 


b) 


c) 


d) 


e) 


g) 


h) 


NOTE — Tappings from the hydrant system to feed water 
spray systems for smaller installations may be permitted by the 
Authority. Pump selection and capacity in such cases shall be 
as per IS 13039. 

Pumps shall be direct coupled except in the case 
of engine driven vertical turbine pumps wherein 
gear drives shall be used. Belt driven pumps shall 
be avoided. 


Parts of pumps like impeller, shaft sleeve, wearing 
ring, etc, shall be ofnon-corrosive metal preferably 
of brass or bronze. 


Where seawater is used or where the quality of the 
water necessitates the use of special metals and 
alloys, the use of such metals and alloys shall be 
insisted upon. 


The rating and design of motors and switchgear 
shall conform to the relevant Indian Standard 
specifications. The motor shall be of continuous 
rating type and its rating shall be equivalent to 
the horse power required to drive the pump at 
150 percent of its rated discharge. Pumps shall be 
chosen with minimum duty parameters as stated in 
Table 8. 


In case of electrically driven pumps, it is required 
to provide a compression ignition engine driven 
stationary pump of similar capacity be installed as 
a standby; and vice versa. 
NOTE — Notwithstanding the above, if power to motorized 
fire pumps is obtained from two sources, one of which is a 
captive generating plant located in a block either 6 m away 
from all surrounding building or, where this is not feasible, 
fire separated from adjoining buildings in a manner indicated 
in 10.3, more than one pump may be of the electrically 
driven type. 
In case of jockey pumps in such systems to take 
care of minor leakages, the capacity thereof shall 
not be less than 3 percent and normally not more 
than 10 percent of the installed pumping capacity. 


Each pump shall be provided with a pressure gauge 
on delivery side between the pump and non-return 
valve and a plate giving delivery head, capacity 
and the number of revolutions per minute.

10.3 Pump Room Location 


a) 


b) 


c) 


d) 


Pumps shall not be installed in the open. The 
pump room shall be so located as to be both easily 
accessible and where any falling masonry and the 
like from other buildings occasioned by fire or 
other causes, cannot damage the pump room. 


Normally, pump rooms shall be located 6 m away 
from all surrounding buildings and overhead 
structures. 


Where this is not feasible, they may be attached to 
a building provided a fire wall having a rating of 
at least 2 h is constructed between the pump room 
and attached building, the roof of pump room is 
of RCC construction at least 100 mm thick and 
access to the pump room is from the outside. 


The pump rooms shall normally have brick/ 
concrete walls and non-combustible roof, with 
adequate lighting, ventilation and drainage 
arrangements. 


IS 15325 : 2020 


e) The pump room shall be located 30 m clear of the 


equipment/vessels handling or storing flammable 
liquids/solvents and/or gases.

NOTE — For high hazard occupancies, substation(s) supplying 
power to fire pumps shall, in addition to complying with the 
above provisions, be located 30 m clear of all equipment where 
flammable fluids having a flash point below 65°C are handled 
and/or stored. 

Overhead feeders to sub-station(s) supplying 
power to the fire pump(s) are not permitted within 
a horizontal distance of: 


1) 15 m of any process building/plant or tanks 
containing flammable liquids, or 


2) 6 m of any other building or tanks containing 
non-flammable liquids or of storage in open. 


In case the feed to such sub-station(s) is by means 
of underground cables, the cables shall not pass 
under any building or permanent structure. 


Sufficient spare power shall always be available 
to drive pumping set(s) at all times throughout the 
year. 


The electric supply to the pumping set(s) shall be 
entirely independent of all other equipment in the 
premises that is even when the power throughout 
the entire premises is switched off, the supply to 
the pump shall continue to be available interrupted. 
This can be achieved by taking the connection for 
the pump(s) from the incoming side of the main 
LT breaker. 


However, in cases where two or more transformers 
and/or sources of supply are connected to a 
common bus bar or where there is provision of 
a bus coupler between the bus bar sections, the 
connection may be taken through the bus bars. 


The fire pump circuit shall be protected at the 
origin by an automatic circuit breaker so set as 
to permit the motor to be overloaded during an 
emergency to the maximum limit permissible 
by the manufacturers. Further, the under voltage 
release/no volt coil of the circuit breaker shall be 
removed. 

NOTE — Where cable lengths are long enough to warrant 
back-up protection, Authorities may insist on provision for 
such a protection. 

It is recommended that telltale lamps which could 
continuously glow when power is available to the 
fire pump(s) circuit be provided and fixed in a 
prominent position, both in the substation and in 
the pump room. 


A direct feeder without any tappings, shall be laid 
from the substation to the pump house. The feeder 
shall be laid underground and shall not pass under 
any building or permanent structure. 


Where there is more than one source of power for 
the operation of pumping set(s) every electrical 
circuit shall preferably be so designed as to ensure 
that when necessary the set(s) continue to operate 
without the manual operation of an emergency 
switch.

a robust bedplate, if of the horizontal type, and 
shall be free from vibration at all variations of 
load. 


The rating and design of motors and switchgear 
shall conform to the relevant Indian Standard 
specifications. The motor shall be of continuous 
rating type and its ratings shall be equivalent 
to the horse power required to drive the pump 
at 150 percent of its rated discharge. 


The motor shall be of totally enclosed type or 
drip proof type, the latter having their air inlets 
and outlets protected with meshed wire panels to 
exclude rodents, reptiles and insects. 


The motor(s) shall be wound for Class B insulation 
preferably for Class E and the windings shall 
be vacuum impregnated with heat and moisture 
resisting varnish and preferably glass fibre 
insulated to withstand tropical conditions. 


Motor(s) wound for high tension supplies shall 
have a suitable fixed warming resistance to 
maintain the motor windings in a dry condition 
at all times and particularly under monsoon 
conditions. The resistance shall be connected to 
the lighting or other equivalent circuit. Also pump 
motor and the switchgear inside pump house 
shall be housed in an enclosure with a degree of 
protection not less than IP 65. 


Heating apparatus shall also be provided when 
necessary for medium tension motor where 
they are located below ground level, in order to 
maintain the motor windings in a dry condition. 
Adequate drainage arrangements shall also be 
provided in the pump house in such cases. 


The incoming cable to the fire pump room 
shall terminate in an isolating switch fuse unit 
incorporating the HRC fuses and where necessary 
provided with a distribution system. 


The starting switchgear for the fire pumps shall 
be suitable for direct on line starting but other 
alternative arrangements are subject to prior 
approval of the authorities concerned. It shall also 
incorporate an ammeter with a clear indication of 
the motor full load current. 

NOTE — Remote controlled starting arrangements are subject 
to prior approval of the authorities concerned. 

Cables for motors and switchgears shall be 
armored or enclosed in heavy gauge screwed steel 
conduit according to conditions. 

It is recommended that the equipment throughout 
be painted fire red (shade no. 536 as per IS 5) and 
suitably marked for identification. 

Necessary spare parts including a set of fuses (in a 
glass fronted box) shall be kept in readiness at all 
times in the pump house. 


35 


IS 15325 : 2020 


NOTE — The wiring for the fire pumps in all installations shall 
be done in accordance with SP 30. 


10.5 Compression Ignition Engine Driven Pumps 


a) Pump room — The pump room shall be artificially 


b 


c 


d 


e 


) 


wm 


© 


nN 


heated, if necessary to maintain the temperature 
of room above 10°C. Adequate ventilation shall 
be provided for the air required for aspiration and 
to limit the temperature rise in the room to 10°C 
above the ambient temperature when the engine is 
on full load. 


Engine — The engine shall be of the compression 
ignition mechanical direct injection type, capable 
of being started without the use of wicks, 
cartridges, heater plugs or ether, at an engine 
room temperature of 7°C and shall accept full load 
within 15 s from the receipt of the signal to start: 


1) Naturally aspirated, supercharged or 
turbocharged and either air or water cooled. In 
case of charged air cooling by means of a belt 
driven fan or of a belt driven auxiliary water 
pump there shall be multiple belts such that 
should half the belts break, the remaining belts 
would be capable of driving the fan or pump. 


2 


a 


Capable of operating continuously on full load 
at the site elevation for a period of 6 h. 


3 


wa 


Provided with an adjustable governor to 
control the engine speed within 10 percent of 
its rated speed under any conditions of load up 
to the full load rating. The governor shall be set 
to maintain the rated pump speed at maximum 
pump load. 


4) Provided with an in-built tachometer to 


indicate the rpm of the engine. 


wa 


5) 
6) 


Provided with a time totalizer (hour counter). 


Any manual device fitted to the engine which 
could prevent the engine starting shall return 
automatically to the normal position. 


Engines, after correction for altitude and ambient 
temperature shall have bare engine horsepower 
rating equivalent to the higher of the following 
two values: 


1) 20 percent in excess of the maximum brake 
horsepower required to drive the pump at its 
duty point; or 

2) Brake horsepower required to drive the pump 
at 150 percent of its rated discharge. 

The coupling between the engine and the pump 

shall allow each unit to be removed without 

disturbing the other. 

Cooling System — The following systems are 

acceptable: 

1) Cooling by water from the discharge of fire 
pump (taken off prior to the pump discharge 
valve) direct into the engine cylinder jackets 


IS 15325 : 2020 


via pressure reducing device to limit the 
applied pressure to a safe value as specified by 
the engine manufacturer. The outlet connection 
from this system shall terminate at least 
150 mm above the engine water outlet pipe 
and be directed into an open tundish so that the 
discharge water is visible. 


2 


wa 


A heat exchanger, the raw water being supplied 
from the fire pump discharge (taken off prior 
to the pump discharge valve) via pressure 
reducing device, if necessary, to limit the 
applied pressure to a safe value as specified 
by the engine manufacturer. The raw water 
outlet connection shall be so designed that 
the discharged water can be readily observed. 
The water in the closed circuits shall not be 
less than that recommended by the engine 
manufacturer. If the auxiliary pump is belt 
driven there shall be multiple belts so that 
should half the belts break, the remaining belts 
shall be capable of driving the pump. 


3) A frame or engine mounted air cooled radiator 
with a multiple belts driven fan from the engine. 
When half the belts are broken the remaining 
belts shall be capable of driving the fan. The 
water in the closed circuit shall be circulated 
by means of the auxiliary pump driven by the 
engine and the capacity of the closed circuit 
shall be not less than that recommended by the 
engine manufacturer. 


4) Direct air cooling of the engine by means of 
multiple belts driven fan. When half the belts 
are broken the remaining belts shall be capable 
of driving the fan. 


NOTE — Incase of systems described above, a failure actuated 
audio-visual alarm shall be incorporated. 


f) Air filtration — The air intake shall be fitted with 
the filter of adequate size to prevent foreign matter 
entering the engine. 


Exhaust system — The exhaust shall be fitted with 
a suitable silencer and the total back pressure shall 
not exceed the engine maker’s recommendation. 
When the exhaust system rises above the engine, 
means shall be provided to prevent any condensate 
flowing into the engine. 


a 


8 


h) Engine shutdown mechanism — This shall be 
manually operated and return automatically to the 
starting position after use. 

j) Fuel system 
1) Fuel — The engine fuel oil shall be of quality 

and grade specified by engine makers. There 
shall be kept on hand at all times sufficient 
fuel to run the engine on full load for 3 h, in 
addition to that in the fuel tank. 


2) Fuel tank — The fuel tank shall be of welded 
steel construction relevant to Indian or 


36 


International Standard for mild steel drums. 
The tank shall be mounted above the engine 
fuel pump; to provide gravity feed unless 
otherwise recommended by the manufacturers. 
The tank shall be fitted with an indicator 
showing the level of fuel in the tank. The 
capacity of the tank shall be sufficient to allow 
the engine to run on full load for: 


i) Light hazard > 1h 
ii) Ordinary hazard > 2h 
iii) High hazard > 3h 


NOTE — Where there is more than one compression 
ignition engine driven pump set, there shall be separate 
fuel tank and fuel feed pipe for each engine. 


3) Fuel feed pipes — Any valve in the fuel feed 
pipe between the fuel tank and the engine shall 
be placed adjacent to the tank and it shall be 
locked in the open position. Pipe joints shall 
not be soldered and plastic tubing shall not be 
used. 


k) Auxiliary Equipment — The following shall be 


m 


har] 


provided: 

1) Sludge and sediment trap, 

2) A fuel level gauge, 

3) An inspection and cleaning hole, 


4) A filter between the fuel tank and fuel pump 
mounted in an accessible position for cleaning, 
and 


5) Means to enable the entire fuel system to be 
bled of air. Air relief cocks are not allowed; 
screwed plugs are permitted. 


Starting Mechanism — Provision shall be made 
for two separate methods of engine starting, 
namely: 


1) Automatic starting by means of a battery 
powered electric starter motor incorporating 
the axial displacement type of pinion, having 
automatic repeat start facilities initiated by 
a fall in pressure in the water supply pipe to 
the spray installation. The battery capacity 
shall be adequate for ten consecutive starts 
without recharging with a cold engine under 
full compression. 

2) Manual starting by crank handle, if engine size 
permits or electric starter motor. 

NOTE — The starter motor used for automatic starting may 


also be used for manual starting provided there are separate 
batteries for manual starting. 


n) Battery charging — The means of charging 


batteries shall be by a 2-rate trickle charger with 
manual selection of boost charge and the batteries 
shall be charged in position. Where separate 
batteries are provided for automatic and manual 
starting the charging equipment shall be capable of

Equipment shall be provided to determine the 
state of charge of the batteries.

with the engine and kept on hand at all times.
